> Operator 2026-10-05 (verbatim in session s20260929T144138-2948413): ddflow should manage any type of documentation together with the user -- README, RESEARCH, TODO, CHANGELOG, ROADMAP, LOGS, SECURITY, whatever -- and any document the user asks for as part of the document task during the workflow, with rules and configuration for how each is managed, formed, and what content must come from the user. Research R-docs-generic (CONFIRMED). GAP: a document type is Python today (8 export kinds; an unknown kind is refused); hand-written documents have no registry, no section schema, no owners, no user-content capture, no drafts, no per-document rules (Rule.globs is never consulted), no doc events; views, instruction blocks and exports use three machineries and three marker dialects. DESIGN: a declarative DOCUMENT TYPE (TOML; shipped, project .ddflow/doctypes/, or [docs.types.<name>]) = target path or collection pattern + genre + owner + skeleton + ordered SECTIONS, each with ownership (generated | human | seeded | draft), a SOURCE (kind:<export kind> | query:<record query> | fragments:<name> | file:<path#anchor> | cmd:<configured command> | ask | draft | static), validation rules and agent guidance; plus TRIGGERS (depends_on code globs, log events, schedule/stale_after, manual). The 8 export kinds become built-in types with one generated section (byte-identical output). BUILDS ON, does not duplicate: P-doc-templates (B-tpl-regions marker grammar, B-tpl-merge 3-way, B-tpl-adopt, B-tpl-views, B-tpl-instructions), P-roadmap, B-export-* (registry, writer, sandbox, eject, redaction), B-export-security-md, B-security-pass-sync, B-docs-stage (docs check, [docs] config, gate evidence), P-schedule (docs-correctness job), B-upgrade (migrations). Order: decide -> spec -> {sources, events} -> ownership -> {interview, drafts, validate, rules} -> obligations -> {workflow, health} -> surfaces -> library -> {onboard, unify} -> acceptance.

## P-docs-search — Search the documentation: fuzzy and relevance-ranked search for the user and the agent, a token-saving retrieval (RAG) interface over MCP, and an index that follows file changes through a throttled update queue

`open` · ████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/10 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-05 (verbatim in session s20260929T144138-2948413): provide the user and the agent fuzzy and relevance search over the documentation and eventually a RAG interface, to save the agent tokens when a documentation search is needed; ddflow should monitor the managed documentation files and, where indexes are kept, update them as soon as possible without killing the tool (an update queue + throttling). Research R-docs-generic. EXISTS: `ddflow search` (TF-IDF over log records, services/search.py) and recall (BM25 FTS5 over log records, infra/store.py) -- neither indexes a single documentation file; no typo-tolerant matching; no chunk-level retrieval; nothing watches files. DESIGN: heading-aware chunks of the managed docs in a SEPARATE derived, git-ignored index (.ddflow/local/docs.db; the log index stays log-only), FTS5 porter + trigram tables fused by reciprocal rank (LIKE fallback without FTS5), textsim rerank, optional embeddings as a companion (off by default, unavailable when absent, never a silent downgrade); budgeted, cited, fenced snippets over MCP with read-by-chunk expansion so an agent never reads a whole file to answer a question; a persisted, coalescing update queue fed by stat scans at opportunistic points, git hooks and a watcher thread in the long-running MCP server, drained by one locked worker under debounce, batch and CPU budgets, yielding to foreground calls; a query never waits on the full queue (the hit list says how far behind it is, and a small queried file is indexed inline). Scope = [docs].check_paths + doc_globs + every doc-type target, minus ignores and generated views unless asked. Order: decide -> chunker -> index -> {search, queue} -> {rag, watch} -> semantic (optional) -> doctypes link -> surfaces -> acceptance.

## P-record-contract — Record-surface contract: one lifecycle, change feed, retrieval registration, relevance-matched context and RAG export for every record kind, built once for goals, principles, rules, decisions, proposals and later kinds

`open` · ████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/10 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-11 (verbatim, also recorded as a session prompt): "make sure all goals and principles and rules follow the principles of the current project - mcp and cli interfaces, add, edit, delete, modify, merge, split, search, context insert, rag export interfaces and functionalities, so the user or the agent can review, edit, delete, modify, split, evidence is logged, sessions are automatically informed for changes, they retrieve brief on session start, and can also search, ask, or automatically receive context which seems to be related to what the session do"

> The contract is decision D-record-surface-contract (rows RC1 to RC12). This phase builds the SHARED mechanisms once, so goals (P-goals), rules (B-rules-onto-record-surface), decisions (P-decisions), proposals and every later record kind consume them instead of growing per-kind versions. Audit (2026-10-11, verified against the code and every task body): record verbs today are list/show/add/edit/remove/search/revise (api/records.py VERBS); merge, supersede and split exist only as API calls (api/defs.py def_merge, def_supersede) or for tasks, no surface offers them and no history or restore verb exists; ddflow search, recall and the MCP resources register each kind by hand (services/search.py KINDS and _DEF_KINDS, infra/store.py RECALL_SOURCES, surfaces/mcp.py RESOURCES), so a new kind is invisible to search/recall until someone edits those; there is no RAG export of records (ddflow export makes human documents); and nothing tells a running session that a rule, decision, principle or goal changed (hooks prompt, pre_tool, post_tool, stop and session_end are wired and handled by _on_nothing; the brief shows state once at start; research gets its own pre-tool injector only in B-rw-context).

> Tasks, in order: B-rc-lifecycle (history, supersede, merge, split, restore on the record surface) -> B-rc-participation (search, recall, context-candidate and resource registration derived from the descriptor); B-rc-changes (the change feed, per-session cursor and its doors) -> B-rc-context (relevance-matched automatic context at prompt, tool and claim time); B-rc-rag-export; then B-rc-conformance (a generated test over every declared kind).

> Placement (operator 2026-10-11): after the P-unify checkpoint, in the core wave, off the upgrade path; the phase waits for B-checkpoint-after-unify through its P-unify need and changes no existing wave's first round. No daemon (D-sched-no-daemon): ddflow answers at the doors a harness already calls.

## P-extension-seams — One light extension seam for sources, sinks and gates: a typed registry in-tree, an out-of-process plugin protocol outside

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/22 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-12 asked whether to rewrite the workflow engines as plugins (pluggy or similar). Research R-plugin-engines (CONFIRMED): do not rewrite; pluggy gives the in-tree seams nothing and adds a runtime dependency and ~7% startup; the fold must stay closed. ## P-perf — Performance: measured budgets, hook latency, import time and the log read path (no rewrite, no second database unless thresholds are crossed)

`open` · ███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 6/33 tasks · 2 abandoned

> Operator request 2026-10-11 (verbatim): "do a research if there is a worth (if not done before the research and everything) to use duckdb in addition or instead of sqlite to index and process the text data, expose it over rag, etc - for performance, functionality, speed, memory footprint reasons. Also check what are the performance bottlenecks of the current ddflow tool, is there any value of rewritting it in a faster programming language, like rust or go?" Evidence: R-perf-duckdb-measured, R-perf-duckdb-facts, R-perf-profile-2026-10-11 (CONFIRMED), R-perf-rewrite-2026-10-11 (THEORETICAL); earlier: D-no-duckdb (binding), R-perf-100k, Rb9e3498a92, R-gaps-evidence. Findings: the bottleneck is algorithmic Python (asdict in the lease fold, 3-6 folds per command, full-log read for every Lamport max, eager import of the whole CLI), not SQLite and not the language. The log-read/fold/Lamport fixes live in B-gap-log-scale (extended 2026-10-11, P-gaps core wave); this phase holds what is NOT there: the operator decisions, the benchmark harness with budgets, the import-time and hook fast paths, MCP start-up and resident cache. Held: nothing here starts before B-perf-decide is answered (recommended defaults in its body). Positioned after P-unify and after the operator pause (B-checkpoint-after-unify). Operator 2026-10-11 (D-perf-core-wave): B-perf-lazy-cli and B-perf-hook-fast-path ride the core wave with P-gaps (hook latency is the most felt cost: prompt hook 1.27 s, session-start 6.0 s, R-perf-profile-2026-10-11); they do not wait for the docs wave or P-decisions. B-perf-mcp-start follows B-gap-log-scale; B-perf-bench follows B-perf-decide and B-gap-log-scale.

## P-change-surface — Small change surface: a feature touches its own files, nothing shared by hand, nothing too big to read

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/28 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-12: minimise the surface, components and shared or managed files a change needs so an LLM adds, changes and reads code faster with fewer bugs and less locking; and (D-small-files) keep every file under 20 KB, source and tests alike, so even a 128k-context model can do a whole change. Research R-change-surface (250 merges: median 6 files, README in 33%, pins in 30%, aggregator files in 13-23 merges each) and R-file-size (57 source files = 48% of source bytes and 43 test files over 20 KB; the 12 largest source files are ~250k tokens; always-loaded context: the tool list is ~24k tokens). Tasks: footprint measurement, pins, aggregators, docs fragments, size ratchet and six source split groups plus waves 2 and 3, two test waves, pins and loaded-docs sizes, smaller code, the always-loaded context budget, codemap, and two research tasks (leases, feature slices). New code in every other phase is written as small modules from the start (rule r-small-files).

## P-lean-start — Lean start: a spawned agent starts under 32K tokens (lean profile 8-16K), contract kept, budget measured and ratcheted

`open` · ██████████░░░░░░░░ 11/20 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-21 verbatim: 'I have noticed that every new agent you spawn (background tasks on claude) immediately starts with 64k tokens taken. Can you investigate how we can optimize the tokens in the beginning of the sessions, still informing the models to ask us for additional information and enforcing what we need, but looking into working with <32K tokens in the beginning of the session at least so we could support models with smaller context windows?' Research: docs/ddflow/research/lean-start.md (R-lean-start-footprint). Measured: as-is 37.2K without ddflow; ddflow adds 3.9K deferred or ~59K undeferred; restricted tools list 25.4K -> 10.4K. Enforcement stays in hooks and gates, the charter only tells the contract. Early tasks (LS-measure, LS-inherit-probe, then LS-charter, LS-agents, LS-worker-mcp-config, LS-launch-brief-budget) need nothing from P-tool-diet or MTD-decision; LS-profile-select and LS-lean-profile wait for MTD-profiles and MTD-search-call.

## P-decisions — Architectural decisions as maintained, checked infrastructure: categories, owners and review dates; executable checks and dependency policy; reminders in brief, reviews, commits and periodic sweeps; waivers; presets and inference; managed on every surface

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/15 tasks · 1 abandoned · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Operator 2026-10-06 (verbatim in session s20260929T144138-2948413): keep and maintain architectural decisions for every project, let the user preset them, let ddflow remind and monitor them wherever they apply, manageable like the rest (CLI, config, add, remove, edit, search, RAG), so decisions about infrastructure, way of coding, libraries, dependencies, upgrades and tests are monitored and maintained per project. Research R-decisions (CONFIRMED). TODAY: a small ADR record (globs, alternatives, supersede-only) reminded in brief/claim by glob overlap; no checks, no review-gate injection, no category/owner/enforcement/review date, no dependency policy, no waivers, no staleness review, no edit or retire, no presets, no inference, ADR files imported once. DESIGN: a decision is a record (on the definition-record model, B-uni-def-records) with category, scope globs, owner, enforcement (advisory|warn|block), review_by and revisit triggers, links, and CHECKS: fitness functions of typed kinds (deps, imports, pattern, files, config, command, radar) evaluated by one engine on the tree or a diff, unavailable never passed. Monitoring points: brief and claim (reminder), review gate prompts (reviewers verify compliance), a task-level 'decisions' gate (mechanical checks on the diff), pre-commit fast checks (manifests, staged files), a periodic sweep job (drift report) and event triggers (manifest changed, decision accepted). A violation is fixed, waived (scoped, time-boxed, approved) or answered with a superseding proposal for the operator. Presets: shipped and company decision packs applied with an interview; onboarding infers current decisions from the codebase as proposals. Every operation on CLI, MCP, a /decide prompt and authored files (.ddflow/decisions/*.toml); recall/search/context packs include decisions; ADR files kept in sync through the ADR document type. BUILDS ON (does not duplicate): B199 (generic edit/retire; this phase extends it for decisions), B-path-rules-to-decisions, B-architecture-pass, B-coh-contradiction, B-rw-vs-decision, B-semantic-recall, B-provenance-remaining-surfaces, B-uni-def-records, B-uni-record-surface, B-uni-cmdrunner, B-uni-approval, B-uni-context-pack, B-uni-kind-pipeline, B-uni-triggers, B-dt-library (ADR collection), P-org-config (company packs, enforced decisions), B-sched-defaults (architecture review job), B-dependency-upgrades. Waits for P-unify (D-unify-first). Order: decide -> model -> {manage, checks} -> {deps, monitor, review, rag} -> waivers -> presets -> {infer, adr-files} -> acceptance.

## P-org-config — Central configuration: a company's defaults and policies (config, workflow, rules, skills, companions, prompts, templates, doc types, schedules) fetched from git or HTTPS, pinned, verified, synced and layered under the project's overrides -- and every configurable thing on every surface, recorded

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/17 tasks · 2 abandoned · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Operator 2026-10-05 (verbatim in session s20260929T144138-2948413): retrieve configuration extensions of config, workflow, rules, skills, companions -- everything configurable -- from git, remote HTTPS or another source, sync them periodically, so a company manages defaults, policies, rules, skills and workflows centrally and the project uses them unless the user overrides; and use the opportunity to ensure parity: everything configurable through MCP, prompt, CLI or config files, and preserved, behind a unified interface; check how similar software does it. Research R-org-config (CONFIRMED). TODAY: no include/extends/remote mechanism; provenance is a layer name; most config writes are not logged; parity gaps listed in R-org-config; agents can loosen policy knobs over MCP. DESIGN: sources [[org.source]] in the project, ~/.config/ddflow/org.toml or /etc/ddflow/org.toml (git+https, git+ssh, https tarball, file, gh:owner/repo//profile@ref); a bundle mirrors .ddflow/ plus manifest.toml and policy.toml; committed .ddflow/org.lock (commit + canonical digest + signer); layers shipped < org defaults < project < local < env/CLI < org ENFORCED (policy kinds pin/floor/ceiling/require/allow, mode enforce|audit -- after Codex requirements.toml, Claude managed settings, Kyverno); per-key merge strategy from knob metadata; data applied once verified, executable content (commands, hooks, MCP launch lines, command reviewers, skill scripts) only after a per-hash operator approval; sources must be on a machine-level allowlist and enforced content must be signed; sync DETECTS upstream changes and proposes a reviewed lock bump (task or PR), never silently applies (except signed enforced policy if the org opts in, recorded); offline runs from the locked cache, enforced policy fails closed; per-value provenance (layer, source, rev, file, line) and config.changed events for every write on every surface. Depends on P-unify (D-unify-first): knob metadata (B-uni-knobs), overlay loader (B-uni-overlay), def-records, record surface and command registry, approval, local worker and trigger engine. Order: decide -> {sources, bundle} -> lock -> trust -> layers -> policy -> {events, provenance} -> {sync, parity, agent-guard} -> kinds -> {authoring, surfaces} -> acceptance.

## P-awareness — Operator awareness: push as well as pull — event notifications, an operator inbox, a digest since you last looked, roadmap progress with an honest estimate

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/9 tasks · 2 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-20: is there planned work for ddflow to give periodic updates and overall roadmap progress so the user knows at any moment what is happening? Audit: PULL exists (ddflow status, board, progress, brief, report --brief, metrics forecast); PLANNED pull: DX-status-digest (ddflow digest), DX-waves-status, B-rm-surfaces (roadmap), P-remote.gateways (compact status over chat apps), GR-wave-derived (depth/wave derived). NOT planned before this phase: periodic digests, event-driven notices (merge landed, gate failed or unavailable, push/CI failed, agent died or idle, phase done, decision needed), a live view, one operator inbox, and a roadmap-level estimate with its uncertainty. Evidence: the operator asked 'what is the status' about 20 times in one day, each answer cost 5-8 commands plus ad-hoc scripts. Design rules: (1) no daemon is required (D-no-daemon-r2): periodic delivery is a command (ddflow digest --notify) run by cron/systemd timer, a hook, or a P-daemon kind the operator starts; (2) every notification class, threshold, quiet-hours window and rate limit is a knob (D-everything-configurable); (3) one sink interface, many sinks (terminal line, file, command, chat gateway); (4) never report what did not run as success: unavailable/partial/forced are shown as such (the B835d22b138 lesson), and an estimate shows its sample size and says 'unknown' when history is too thin; (5) reuse DX-status-digest, DX-waves-status, GR-wave-derived, the cadence machinery and P-remote.gateways instead of building parallel versions; (6) new commands are declared with family and action for the MCP tool diet (D-mcp-tool-families), not as new flat tools; (7) notifications never contain private addresses, hostnames or keys (D-event-log-redaction-forward).

## P-devcontainer — Devcontainers: no docker-in-docker for companions, ddflow verified to work in a devcontainer, and a published devcontainer Feature that installs ddflow

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/11 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-20: (1) the codeguide-mcp companion must be recommended as the public remote MCP server, not a local docker pull, so a devcontainer never needs docker-in-docker (D-codeguide-remote-default); (2) investigate whether ddflow works well in devcontainers and what has to change; (3) produce devcontainer Features for ddflow in the GitHub pipeline and publish them (GHCR, listed in the containers.dev features index) so ddflow can be added to any devcontainer automatically. Known risks to test, not assume: .claude/settings.json and hooks record absolute interpreter paths of the machine that wrote them (doctor already warns they dangle elsewhere); git worktrees and flock on bind mounts / virtiofs / overlayfs; UID mapping and git safe.directory; ddflow next folds a 65 MB log, slow on mounts; adaptive parallelism and pytest -n auto read host cores/load, not the container's cgroup limits; /proc/locks visibility in a PID namespace; .ddflow/local and secrets do not survive a container rebuild unless in a volume or remoteEnv; LAN reviewer hosts and roborev/kilo reachability from the container network; the pre-commit golang gitleaks build needs go. Publishing is outward-facing: the GHCR package and the containers.dev index submission need the operator's go-ahead (DCF-collection-index is an operator step). Reuse ddflow.infra.container.in_container, the mcpconfig registration, the harness descriptors and the existing publish workflow; do not build a second install path.

> NOTE 2026-10-20: the research task is DCF-research (renamed from RC-devcontainer-research, RC- is the record-contract prefix). Read 'RC-devcontainer-research' in the task bodies as DCF-research; tasks it files use the DCF- prefix too.

> Research note R-roadmap-review (graph analysis). Each task below is an engine that several phases were about to build separately. Every consumer gets a dependency edge to its engine, so the engine lands first and the consumers shrink to configuration and data.

> Rules: defaults change nothing; no new phase task writes README.md, ddflow/config.py, ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py or ddflow/core/events.py by hand (registries and generated regions only); everything configurable, small files, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged. Filed per D-usage-pacing-2026-10.

## P-graph — Graph foundations: one effective edge set, a cached import graph, impact queries; stdlib only, no new subsystem

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/14 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-19: research graph engineering for AI agents; where does it help ddflow, and file the phase if useful. Research (three reports, /tmp/claude-1001/research/graph-landscape.md, graph-internal.md, graph-codegraph.md; committed copies via DX-commit-research-reports): ddflow is already the graph (event log + needs + leases + gates); the scheduling graphs are cheap (plan 0.12 s, critical_path 0.02 s, waves 0.63 s on 2735 items; ddflow next is 2.6 s of which 1.7 s is reading and folding the 65 MB log, so B-perf-mcp-start matters more than any graph cache). Worth building: (1) ONE effective edge set on State (six+ bugs came from readiness, critical_path, progress and the restamp scripts each re-deriving it: B27, B67, B79c2f6e17a, B13ed484062, Bbbcbfc4bbb, B43447abfc8); (2) a persisted import graph (testreach.build re-parses 1487 files in 5.6 s on every selection) keyed by blob hash; (3) one impact query that P-context-sync.impact, .prompt, .conflict, PD-baseline, CN-consumers and B-dec-monitor each otherwise reimplement; (4) wave/depth as a derived attribute instead of hand-stamped wave:N tags; (5) impact-aware review scope. DELIBERATELY NOT built (revisit only with evidence): GraphRAG or knowledge-graph agent memory (ICLR 2026 study: frequently underperforms vanilla RAG; Zep gains 1.4 points on DMR, vendor-measured), SCIP/CodeQL/Sourcegraph indexers (external dependencies, D-graph-stdlib), full reverse-import closure for test selection (median module reaches 459 of 810 tests, core/records.py 92%), incremental ready/wave maintenance (saves ~0.1 s), a unified typed property graph over items+records+files+symbols, decision relevance by graph distance. Policy D-graph-stdlib stands: stdlib graphlib plus core/graph; networkx only as a dev-only test oracle. Extend core/graph and services/testreach.py; do not add a second graph engine. Success is measured, not argued: GR-acceptance.

> NOTE: this report now lives at docs/ddflow/research/graph-codegraph.md, docs/ddflow/research/graph-internal.md, docs/ddflow/research/graph-landscape.md, docs/ddflow/research/scripts/graph_probe.py

## P-reasoning — A thin native reasoning log (typed steps, ruled-out hypotheses, revisions) in place of the external sequential-thinking companion -- built only if it measures as worth it

`open` · ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/9 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator request 2026-10-10: investigate the `sequential` companion (the MCP Sequential Thinking server) and, if sensible, bring the part that makes sense into ddflow instead of recommending an external tool. Evidence: research R-reasoning-sequential. The server computes nothing and returns no thought text; it keeps counters and a history array in its own process that dies with it. Its one real idea -- a revision/branch-marked scratchpad where what was RULED OUT stays visible -- is what ddflow's bug_hunt, research and rubber_duck gates want, but a second unversioned, unsearchable scratchpad outside the log splits reasoning into two places and loses it at context exhaustion.

> Scope: a THIN native reasoning log, not a clone. Typed steps (question, hypothesis, evidence, ruled_out, decision), revision/branch links, tied to an item and a gate, redacted, searchable, cited, fed into the existing research record / gate evidence (never a second research artifact), readable by cross-family reviewers as fenced data, with a budget, a repeat guard and an off switch. Then MEASURE it on real ddflow work (B-rs-eval) and keep it only if it earns its place; the external companion is demoted to optional-superseded only after that.
> Do NOT build: a tool that 'thinks' for the model, a visualiser, a general memory (P-agent-memory owns that).

## P-pipeline-ideas — Default-pipeline ideas mined from five Claude skills: document class and review cursor, terminology, claims review, scenario cards, review lenses and panels, all as configuration and shipped templates

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/11 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-11 (verbatim): "Look at these skills for claude, are there ideas we could take advantage from, and extend the functionality of the ddflow tool, if such functionality or capability is missing, or impossible to implement with the current capabilities?" and, clarifying: "the idea is those skills to give us ideas for our default workflow if those ideas are worth it. How to manage skills and subagents and integrate those in our workflow is a separate development phase ... Do not add those skills to this project, just read the content and think of generic ideas that worth to be implemented in our default pipeline, but do follow the principles of this project - nothing have to be hardcoded - everything should be possible to configure, change, remove, change order, constants, variables, pipelines, workflows should be configurable, changeable, written as config (if modified default behavior) and able to be shared, managed by the user, ddflow cli or the agents, including via mcp interface".

> Research R-skills-mining-gaps (CONFIRMED: what exists, what is planned, what is missing) and R-skills-mining-value (THEORETICAL: whether the ideas pay off). Skills read: e2e-scenario-testing, maintaining-documentation, mcp-cli, roborev-design-review, roborev-design-review-branch. Nothing here installs, generates or manages skills or subagents; that is P-skills and P-subagents (their authoring conventions are only noted there as input).

> WHAT THIS PHASE ADDS (only what no existing task covers; everything else in the skills is already built or planned and was extended in place with a 'Skills-mining extension 2026-10-11' paragraph): (1) a persisted CLASS per document (evergreen | point_in_time | generated) that every docs check, gate and auto-fix honours, confirmed by the operator; (2) a review CURSOR per document (doc.reviewed: sha, verifier, deferred claims) so re-audits are incremental and an unverified claim never rides under a clean review; (3) a claims-versus-reality review gate whose evidence checks the VERB (the code path that enacts a claim), not the noun; (4) a terminology dictionary; (5) corpus-level docs checks (duplication, gaps, contradictions, unregistered documents); (6) scenario cards: agent-executed markdown tests with falsifiers, run as a gate and a scheduled sweep; (7) the review LENS as data per gate (today a code constant) with design, security and docs-claims lenses; (8) an optional reviewer PANEL with a synthesis record.

> HOW EVERYTHING IS CONFIGURABLE: each item is data on an existing engine (document-type TOML, [docs.*] and [review.*] config sections, GateDef entries in .ddflow/gates.toml or the shipped built-ins, schedule job templates, definition records), editable by CLI and MCP, shareable through org bundles, removable or reorderable in the pipelines, and off or advisory by default so no existing project changes behaviour on upgrade. Invariants stay the floor: unavailable is never passed, cross-family review, failing-first for bugs, human gates not clearable over MCP.

> B-pi-decide asks the operator first; nothing else here starts before the answers.

## P-agent-memory — Agent memory: capture, hand off, search and remind across context restarts and pipelines

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/15 tasks · 1 abandoned · needs `P-decisions`, `P-org-config`

> Operator question 2026-10-10: do we log and store everything sent to a pipeline's agent, summarise before a context-exhaustion restart and log the summary, hand the restarted agent that summary plus search over its own and other pipelines' old context, expose search/review/dump to the operator on CLI and MCP, and remind agents of past failures so bugs and loops do not repeat? Research R-agent-memory: today only operator prompts, a few notes and one-line session summaries are logged; lane briefs, lane reports, tool traffic and transcripts are not; PreCompact records a pre-compaction tail (and its hook is not installed here); the harness's real compaction summary is never read; session search is BM25 over prompts/notes only; no session search/timeline/diff/dump tools; loop detectors never look at repeated commands or refusals. This phase closes those gaps ONLY by reusing the P-unify components (sessions, searchcore SearchSource, contextpack Budget, redact profiles, LocalStore, def-records, upcasters, command registry, guidance inject, ticks). B-am-decide asks the operator the design choices first; nothing else is built before the answers.

> Operator 2026-10-05: hooks, prompts, onboarding and features must work on all supported agents (Claude, Copilot, Codex, Gemini, opencode, Kilo, Qwen Code, Aider, Windsurf, Antigravity, Cursor, Cline/Roo, Goose, Amp, ...), and adding one later must not mean rewriting code. ## P-agent-compat — Every agent and bot we support is tested for real: tiers and a capability matrix, MCP protocol tests, live-recorded fixtures, headless smoke runs per agent, bot sandbox tests, a compatibility report and issue tracking -- including Grok Build

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/14 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-08 (verbatim in session s20260929T144138-2948413): does ddflow support grok and grok bots among the other agents it is supposed to support; prepare a phase with tasks that test the support and work, integration and issues with all the coding agents and bots we want to support. Research R-agent-compat (CONFIRMED): Grok has one drivable surface, the official Grok Build CLI (plus a community twin); Grok elsewhere is a model inside host agents; bots divide into stdio-capable runner agents, remote-only or instructions-only cloud agents, review bots and event sources. Builds on P-harness-adapters (descriptors, hook core, writers, fixture conformance, research matrix) and does not duplicate it: that phase makes a new agent data; this phase proves with a real run, per agent and bot, that it works, keeps proving it as vendors change, and reports it. Layers: tiers and criteria; MCP protocol tests without an LLM; live-recorded fixtures; headless smoke runs with flakiness controls and 'unavailable' for a missing key/CLI/rate limit (never pass); bot sandbox runs (advisory); a compatibility report with versions and dates; issues filed against ddflow or upstream. Waits for P-unify (D-unify-first).

## B-adaptive-flow — Adaptive flow: the number of agents in flight adjusts itself to what is safe, by default, configurable

`open` · ██████████░░░░░░░░ 9/16 tasks · 1 abandoned · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'When conflicts are removed you could raise this is - again make it default for ddflow, but also make sure it is configurable by config, cli, mcp so the user has control. Is it possible to investigate flow control options where these limits are dynamically managed depending on capabilities and availabilities - the goal is the project to auto adjust to the maximum that is safe available safely to work : Raising max_parallel_tasks: this only helps once conflicts are removed. Ready, unblocked items are down to two.' Research R-task-time (extended by inv-flow): the DAG plus globs allowed a mean 24 more conflict-free items while in-flight averaged 1.86 of a cap of 4; only 58% of offered items were mutually independent; the cap is advisory (claim does not check it). Decision D-adaptive-flow (PROPOSED: the operator confirms its choices before B-af-config onward is claimed). Order: B-af-offer (conflict-aware offering, no-regret, independent of the rest) and B-af-core, then config, signals, sampler, wiring, slots, surfaces, doctor, docs. Related: B-hot-files (the real cure for glob blocking), B-lease-edit-only-hold, B-reviewer-pool, B-review-budget-*, B-quota-*.

## P-agent-parity — Agent parity: the same ddflow behaviour on every coding agent, ddflow in charge of when to stop, a shared launcher, measured by a behavioural suite

`open` · ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 3/32 tasks · 3 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-12: Kilo lacks what Claude has (hooks, session records, task monitoring, and it stops after every task until the user says continue instead of letting ddflow decide); make the behaviour and features identical on every agent on the market, fill the gaps, extend or reuse existing phases. Research R-agent-parity (CONFIRMED) from four primary-source reports and probes. Extends, does not duplicate: P-harness-adapters (descriptor, hook core, writers, generic onboarding, identity, cli, conformance), P-agent-compat (D-agent-compat tiers, smoke, fixtures, matrix), P-agent-hygiene (stop protocol, B-hy-kilo-onboard), P-agent-memory (transcripts), P-governor (meters, restart, tiers), P-agent-lifecycle (detect, verify, redo, offboard), P-agent-caps (groups). New pieces: a continuation engine, a headless launcher, descriptor sections, a no-hook wrapper, permission profiles, tool-count profiles, MCP client compatibility, drift watch and a parity suite. Every number and command template is a knob (D-everything-configurable).

## P-ai-import — Import existing AI workflow: scan, inventory, dedupe and convert the instructions, rules, skills, subagents, commands, hooks, MCP and permissions a project already has, for every supported agent, then manage them from ddflow with drift detection and revert

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/31 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-13: when ddflow is onboarded on a project with a preexisting AI workflow, skills, agent specs and rules, how are they imported and managed from then on, for all supported coding agents, so the operation after onboarding is smooth; what exists, what to extend.

> Research note R-ai-config-import (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline/Roo/Kilo, opencode, Aider, Continue and others; paths for several agents are unverified and are probed first). Exists or planned today and extended, not duplicated: rules inventory and import (B-rules-inventory, B-rules-import), skills model, onboarding and sync (B-skills-*), subagent parse, onboarding and sync (B-sub-*), agent command adoption (B-adopt-agent-commands), instruction blocks and the region engine (B-tpl-*), the install manifest, verify, redo and offboard of P-agent-lifecycle, harness descriptors (P-harness-adapters, P-agent-parity.descriptor-v2), decision inference at onboarding (B-dec-infer). Gaps: ONE inventory and normalisation across all artifact classes, the who-loads-what graph, contradiction and duplicate detection, plan/apply/backup/revert, digest manifests with drift and round-trip, hazard scans, and the per-agent adapters.
> Design: read-only scan then a human inventory; deterministic classification first, an LLM only to split monolithic files (a proposal, trust=agent); canonical records with extra.<harness> fields; AGENTS.md canonical and pointers instead of copies where the harness allows; copy-sync with managed markers and digests elsewhere; permissions, hooks, plugins, off-disk team rules and specs stay native-only records with a pointer and digest; the import is a plan applied as a queue item with its own worktree and gates, and is revertable; user edits outside managed regions are never touched.
> Rules: nothing is overwritten without a backup; a contradiction blocks adopt until a decision; imported text is trust=imported data; a secret or hidden-Unicode hit blocks emit; user-scope files are hashed, never copied into the repo; everything configurable, small files, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged. Paced per D-usage-pacing-2026-10.

## P-agent-caps — Parallelism caps per coding agent under a global cap, with bookable expiring slots

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/8 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-12: a cap per coding agent (claude, kilo, cursor...) on the same repo and computer, obeying one global cap, by default 80% of it each so several agents run side by side and share capacity; a tool to book and release a slot centrally; slots expire by default and are kept alive by the agent, so dead agents are released automatically. ## P-reshape — Reshape the queue: rename ids, move tasks between phases, reorder

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/11 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-12, from the home-simulator upgrade: phase PHASE-39-FOLLOW-UPS-NOT and tasks P42.8.give-base-room-bluep and P42.8.model-alexas-cloud-g have mangled (truncated) ids; ddflow has no way to rename an id or move a task to another phase, so the upgrade agent left them. Add the means to correct such records: rename an id of any kind (phase, task, bug, decision, lesson, research...) with every reference rewritten (needs, parent, phase, gates, leases, links, bugs fix-<id>, worktree/branch names); move a task (and its sub-tasks) to another phase; reorder phases and tasks; and a repair the upgrade can propose for truncated ids. The event log is append-only and committed, so all of it must be new events folded by the model, never an edit of history.

## P-daemon — Managed daemons: ddflow may start, stop, monitor, attach to and detach from long-running helper processes, within a declared list and a policy, with the operator told

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/10 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-14 (D-roadmap-review, verbatim): 'I want to explore the option of ddflow to be able to start daemon if it decides, in addition to the operator, with notification to the operator, unless this is forbidden by config, or policy, and ddflow to be able manage the daemon life stages, start, stop, monitor, attach, disconnect, etc - whatever is expected'. Policy chosen: config lists the daemon kinds ddflow may start itself (allowed by default for that list); every start is logged and shown in brief and notification sinks; config, policy or [daemon].auto=off forbids; a kind not on the list needs the operator. Research first; D-sched-no-daemon is amended by the decision that follows the research. Reuses the long-running job engine (ddflow job), leases and heartbeats, P-remote.serve, P-schedule (watch, executor-basic), CP-backend-tmux, CP-notify-sinks, P-remote.events (follow), doctor and the approvals engine. CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core, r-small-files): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12 (add, edit, remove as a tombstone, review and history, search, recall and RAG export, logged events and replay restore); every shipped default is overridable per project and per org; search for an existing function and extend the shared engines (P-shared-engines) instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB.

Builds on, never duplicates: P-subagents (registry, sync, route, separation of duties, trust, metrics), P-skills (model, events, authoring, sync, doctor, context), the rules machinery (shipped CRUD, injected by glob), P-record-contract (one lifecycle for every kind), P-governor (tiers, quotas, floors), B-gap-spend (usage ledger) and P-agent-parity (hook rungs per harness). ## P-stack-tools — Stack probe and assurance tools: detect the project's stack, propose per-stack linters, types, contracts, provers, LSP and AST servers, security and mutation tools and rule servers as companions, accepted by the agent or operator and used by every workflow

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/19 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-13: is Creusot worth adding; should ddflow manage such tools (contracts, validation, LSP, AST, ruff) as companions by stack, probing the stack and using the agent plus internet to propose, then agent or operator accepts; codeguide could provide rules and styles per stack; useful for research and test workflows and anything planned; extend current core and planned tasks; add tasks for the rest.

> Research note R-stack-tools. Decision: yes, as a probe + catalogue + proposal flow; Creusot is an opt-in verifier named by a workflow, not a default gate (v0.14.0, Why3 and SMT solvers, needs opam; Kani is the better first Rust verifier: cargo install --locked kani-verifier). Value order: configured linters, dependency and licence checks, type checkers, faster test runners (also helps the unit_tests gate timeout), LSP MCP servers (advisory), shell/Docker/IaC linters, Kani or CBMC, property tests, mutation on changed code, ast-grep or Opengrep rules.
> Reuse: the existing companions registry and ddflow companions add (extended, not replaced), decision inference at onboarding (B-dec-infer: ONE stack detector), org bundles (companions.toml), the style and API cards and the consult action (P-safeguards), the approvals engine and data-declared kinds (P-shared-engines), the pre-commit companion work (B-precommit-integration), dependency and security upkeep (B-dependency-upgrades, B-security-pass), tool version watches (P-schedule.watch-sources), test kinds and mutation adapters (P-test-flows), vendor-tool allowlist (P-test-domains), workflow verifier slots (P-research-flows), format checkers (P-constellation). All of them name tools from ONE catalogue instead of keeping their own lists.
> NEW: the stack probe command, the catalogue data per stack, the proposal and accept flow, the agent-plus-internet step, install-safety rules, the anti-gaming counters (suppressions, config edits, trusted or assumed markers) and the LSP and AST companion wiring.
> Rules: nothing is installed without an accepted proposal and ddflow prints the install command and never runs it; a declined tool leaves its gate unavailable, never passed; agent-proposed entries are trust=agent, verified false, cited; new MCP servers get their tool descriptions hashed at accept time; an agent may not weaken a tool config, tests or specs alongside the code they check unseen by review; everything configurable, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged. Paced per D-usage-pacing-2026-10.

## P-observe — Self-observation and self-improvement: detect, interpret with the LLM, propose at the right moments, apply within bounds, measure the effect

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/16 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-12: ddflow should self-monitor and self-observe, with the help of the LLM and agents, detect bugs, defects, inefficiency and deviations per project workflow, propose improvements (to the project, the way of work and the workflow) when research ends, when a phase starts or ends, and periodically, and optimise itself: workflow, quality, cost. Research R-observe (CONFIRMED). Reuses and extends, not duplicates: P-goals (B-prop-model proposal record, B-prop-discover periodic discovery, B-goal-report acceptance numbers), P-schedule (jobs, triggers, escalation), P-gaps (B-gap-metrics), B-adaptive-flow (the AIMD pattern), P-governor (tier feedback), P-lessons (effect), P-safeguards (cost), P-change-surface (footprint), P-coherence (contradictions), P-configurable (logged config changes). Principles: deterministic detection first, the LLM interprets and proposes with cited evidence and a cross-family check, the operator decides, auto-tuning only inside operator-set bounds with automatic rollback, everything logged, every number a knob.

## P-control-planes — Control-plane integrations: drive ddflow from Paseo, AgentOS, Harness Remote, Nimbalyst, Orca, Emdash and other agent control planes (MCP profiles, adopt-claims, lane backends, ACP wrapper, attention items, scoped tokens)

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/28 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-13: look over Paseo and research how easy it is to integrate ddflow so it is managed remotely with any of the supported Paseo agents; find features and gaps beyond what is planned; same for AgentOS, Harness Remote, Nimbalyst, Orca, Emdash; reuse existing cores.

> Research note R-control-planes. Verdicts: Paseo is the best fit and the first target (SDK over WebSocket, CLI, plugins, per-agent MCP injection, ACP provider, permission model); AgentOS and Emdash are easy for MCP, notify and setup hooks; Harness Remote is mostly a transfer-pack rendering; Nimbalyst is a one-way mirror; Orca is a medium lane backend. The worktree-ownership conflict is the main design problem. Unverified (probes are the first task): Paseo lifecycle hook names, project .mcp.json support and adoption of a pre-made worktree; Harness Remote's API; whether ACP adapters honor an injected MCP server and cwd; adoption in AgentOS, Orca, Emdash.
> Reuse: ddflow serve, auth, events, ask and gateways (P-remote), the lane launcher, descriptors and parity suite (P-agent-parity), spawn engine, notify and context (P-spawn), the lane ledger (done), transfer packs (B-sc-transfer), memory handoff (B-am-handoff), the typed registry (P-extension-seams), the existing external sync and harness-worktree recognition, cost envelopes (P-safeguards).
> NEW: adopt-claim for foreign worktrees, foreign ids in the ledger, a conflict doctor, the lane-backend interface with backends, the ACP wrapper, an attention-items API, push feed and idempotency, scoped tokens, renderers, competing attempts, intake webhooks, integration kits.
> Rules: ddflow never deletes a worktree it did not create (owner=external); a Paseo or Orca session is a lane with a foreign id, never a second identity; tokens are scoped per item and lane, additive, revocable, loopback by default; no relay is built (document SSH, Tailscale or the Paseo relay); a missing control plane is unavailable, never passed; everything configurable, small files, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged. Paced per D-usage-pacing-2026-10.

## P-acp — ACP: ddflow as an Agent Client Protocol client (lane driver for about 20 agents), registry-driven launch, permission broker, event mapping, continuation loop, and the wrap proxy

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/23 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-13: does it make sense for ddflow to implement ACP to communicate with and control agents; if so propose a phase and tasks.

> Research note R-acp. Verdict: yes, as a client first, then the wrap proxy; no as an ACP agent; remote HTTP/WebSocket later. ACP is the lowest common denominator with the broadest reach (native in gemini, copilot (preview), kilo, cursor, kimi, opencode, qwen, devin, cline, goose, junie, augment, grok; adapters for claude, codex, amp, pi, glm; droid and antigravity have ACP modes; no ACP found for qodo, tabnine, aider, replit, cody, roo, continue, windsurf, vscode); native APIs beat it on fidelity for claude, codex and opencode, so ACP is a generic backend beside native ones, chosen per agent by a knob.
> Reuse: the lane-backend interface, foreign ids and the ACP wrap task (P-control-planes: CP-backend-iface, CP-foreign-ids, CP-acp-wrap), the launcher, descriptors and continuation engine (P-agent-parity), spawn and notify (P-spawn), the approvals engine, capability envelope, event registry and evaluation harness (P-shared-engines, P-safeguards), the agent lifecycle verify (P-agent-lifecycle).
> NEW: the ACP transport and v1 client, the registry reader, the update-to-event mapper, the permission broker, the turn loop, process lifecycle handling, steering, resume, the fake ACP agent and client fixtures, and the conformance run of the wrap proxy.
> Rules: v1 only; advertise no fs or terminal capabilities; every permission request is decided by policy and logged; auth stays with the agent's own login; adapter versions are pinned from the registry and recorded; a missing or unauthenticated agent is unavailable, never passed; everything configurable, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged. Paced per D-usage-pacing-2026-10.

## P-platform-mcp — Agent platform APIs: Kilo MCP and the similar hosted surfaces (Devin, GitHub Copilot, Jules, Codex, Cursor) as guarded lane backends, usage meters and profile stores, plus ddflow's own search-and-call facade

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/17 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-13: check the new Kilo MCP feature; decide if it is worth using in ddflow; if so add it to the agent support and check for similar features for the other agents.

> Research note R-platform-mcp. Decision: yes, opt-in and guarded. Kilo's server (https://mcp.kiloapps.io/mcp, authenticate with kilo mcp auth kilo) gives two tools (search, call) over its API: usage and spend by feature, day and month; agent profiles and variables; cloud agent lifecycle. Similar surfaces were found for Devin, GitHub Copilot (through the GitHub MCP server), Jules (REST alpha), Codex (codex mcp-server), Cursor (Cloud Agents API) and Claude Code (Remote Control).
> Reuse: harness descriptors (P-agent-parity.descriptor-v2), the lane-backend interface and control-plane work (P-control-planes), meters and the spend ledger (P-agent-parity.meters, B-gap-spend, P-governor), canonical subagent and skill sync (B-sub-sync, B-skills-sync), the MCP guard (B-sub-mcp-guard), the approvals engine and the MCP budget reporter (P-shared-engines), the fixtures and fake approach of the evaluation harness.
> NEW: a [platform] descriptor section, per-platform adapters, usage-meter readers, profile sync, the guard rules for platform tools, and a ddflow search-and-call facade.
> Rules: opt-in per project (an adopt entry is written disabled until the operator enables it); tokens never stored in the repo or log, authentication stays with the agent's own flow; the platform acts as the user, so deletes, spend and cross-org actions need an approval and the org is always explicit; returned text is fenced data; everything configurable, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged. Paced per D-usage-pacing-2026-10.

## P-research-flows — Research workflows: pre-registered plans, hypotheses and predictions, verifier-first runs, stop rules, audited evidence and shipped default workflows per domain, standalone or inside a development phase

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/45 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-13: explore ddflow managing research of any kind (architecture, programming, math, electronics, hardware, signal processing, science): research, follow goals and principles, hypotheses, contradictions, tests, validation, choose paths to explore, proofs, repeat until it settles on the best solution, with the agent's help; standalone or as phases of development; default workflows per task type with their own skills, subagents, pipelines and rules; results recorded and reusable. Reuse as much as possible of the existing and planned core.

> Design: research note R-research-flows (web research, 8 default workflows, ranked ideas). Almost everything is an existing or planned engine, configured as data:
> - stages = the per-kind gate pipeline ([gates].kind_pipelines.research) with command/agent gates, reviewer family;
> - hypotheses, predictions, observations, ruled-out results = reasoning-log steps (P-reasoning: B-rs-model, B-rs-cmd);
> - evidence, sources, grades, validity, checks, independent verification = claims (P-research: B-rw-claims, B-rw-sources, B-rw-checks, B-rw-verify);
> - the pre-registered plan and the report = document types (P-docs-generic) with the sha stamp / review cursor (B-pi-doc-reviewed);
> - runs and observations = jobs and scenario records (B-pi-scenario-run, job add); the skeptic = review lens (B-pi-review-lens); roles and skills = subagent defaults and safeguards (B-sub-defaults, P-safeguards); budgets = cost envelopes (P-safeguards.envelope); re-verification = watches (P-schedule.watch); reuse = research inject/query and the record-contract context and RAG export; sharing = org bundles.
> NEW code is only: the workflow template format and its pipeline generator, the plan/prediction ordering rule, the run record wrapper, the stop-rule evaluator, the citation and number audit gate, and the shipped workflow data.

> Rules in force: everything configurable (D-everything-configurable), small files (D-small-files), CLI + MCP + prompt from one declaration, logged as events, nothing runs a verifier that is not on the operator's allowlist, an unavailable verifier is recorded unavailable, never passed. Paced per D-usage-pacing-2026-10: filed now, started after the usage reset.

## P-test-flows — Test workflows: every kind of test (unit to chaos, hardware, UI, deployment, CI/CD, load, mutation, scientific) as data, tests as Markdown cards, filtered generation, mutation and flake control, traceability and test-only repositories

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/36 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-13: research and plan workflows and pipelines for tests of every kind (unit, application, integration, acceptance, hardware in the loop, UI, deployment, CI/CD pipeline validation, load, performance, scalability, resiliency, redundancy, mutation, scientific), tests written and maintained as Markdown in the repo unless the user says otherwise, agent-managed ddflow pipelines for tests inside a bigger job or in repositories that hold only tests; best practices from the internet, LLM use, skills, subagents; reuse as much of the existing and planned core as possible.

> Evidence and design: research note R-test-workflows. Principle: a test kind is a DATA row (runner, oracle, cadence, environment needs, stop rule), the gates and records are the existing ones.
> Reuse: unit_tests and live_test gates, the flake log (ddflow tests --flakes), gate verify and the mutation sample (U4), affected-test selection (B-gap-affected-tests), scenario card, gate and sweep (B-pi-scenario-*: tests as Markdown that an agent runs), document types (P-docs-generic), claims and their executable checks (B-rw-claims, B-rw-checks), the review lens (B-pi-review-lens), subagent roles and safeguard envelopes (P-subagents, P-safeguards), the promotion pipeline for deployments ([flow].environments), scheduled jobs (P-schedule), the live agent harness and fixtures (P-agent-compat), one typed registry (P-extension-seams.registry). The research phase P-research-flows defines a run record; this phase and that one share ONE run-record shape (whichever is built first, the other extends it).
> NEW code is only: the test-kind registry and pipeline generator, the test result record (JUnit ingest, SUT pin, repeats, seed), the read-only-tests rule and assertion-change diff gate, the generated-test filter chain, mutation/flake/selection adapters, traceability view, and shipped data (kinds, cards, workflows, roles).
> Rules: everything configurable, small files, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged; absent tool, bench or runner is unavailable, never passed; no verifier command runs unless allowlisted by the operator; chaos and production-touching tests need an explicit human grant. Paced per D-usage-pacing-2026-10: filed now, started after the usage reset.

## P-product-docs — Requirements, vendor and product documents: sourced and linted requirements, vendor and contract records, quarantined vendor material, product docs generated from records, reviewed pipelines that never send, sign or spend

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/22 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-13: investigate ddflow writing requirements (project, vendors, code) from research, and managing vendor-relationship and product-management documentation as part of the pipeline; what exists and is planned, what to reuse, agent cooperation, best practice and what other tools do, subagents, rules and policies.

> Research note R-product-docs. Spec-driven tools (Spec Kit, Kiro, OpenSpec, BMAD, Tessl) are markdown and diffable but none shows independent-model spec review, regression-test rules, a lessons loop, or vendor and PM document types: that is the gap ddflow's gates fill.
> Reuse (no second engine): structured items as definition-record kinds on the record contract (the pattern of goal, claim and proposal: B-goal-model, B-prop-model, P-record-contract); narrative documents as document types with generated regions (P-docs-generic, region engine); deterministic lint as data on the docs-check engine (B-dt-validate, P-pipeline-ideas terminology and claims review); traceability and suspect links on claims and anchors (B-rw-claims, TF-trace); sources checked mechanically (B-rw-sources); goals as the parents of requirements (P-goals); decisions as links (decision records); person-only adopt for agent proposals (B-prop-model, D-reviewer-trust); trust=external fencing and the capability envelope (P-safeguards); cadenced jobs for dates (P-schedule); operator questions as blocking items (B-am-operator-qa); version cut and completed tasks for release notes.
> NEW code is only: the requirement and vendor record kinds with their lifecycle, the requirement lint rule set (EARS and smells) as data, hash-based suspect links and baselines, the quarantine store and the extract-with-quote step, computed scoring (RICE) and notice deadlines, and the shipped data (document types, roles, workflows).
> Hard rules: a requirement has a source or stays proposed-by-agent; a person accepts it; the agent never sends, signs, accepts terms or commits spend and only drafts; vendor material is untrusted data, stored by reference and hash, never quoted into events, lessons or decisions when confidential; dates and scores are computed in code, not by the model. Everything configurable, small files, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged. Paced per D-usage-pacing-2026-10 unless the operator says otherwise.

## P-test-domains — Test domains: BDD and Robot suites, telecom conformance (TMF, MEF, 3GPP 5G/NTN/6G, O-RAN), packet-network tests (config, BGP, MPLS, traffic) and FPGA/HDL verification on the shared test engines

> Operator 2026-10-13: research BDD tests and tools like Robot, executing TMF, MEF, 3GPP (5G, NTN, 6G) and other conformance tests; network configuration tests, packet networking including BGP and MPLS; FPGA, Verilog, VHDL, SystemVerilog systems and code; what features ddflow needs if a project needs them.

> Research note R-test-domains (snippet-level evidence; gaps listed in the note). This phase EXTENDS P-test-flows (test result record, kind registry, pins, environments, traceability, cards, mutation); it adds no second runner. > Rules: an inconc, error, skip or licence failure is unavailable, never passed; a run without its pins satisfies no gate; vendor tools run only from the operator's allowlist with fixed argument templates; no waveform, pcap or log goes into git or events (reference and hash); generated configs and RTL need a deterministic verifier before any review and the testbench author differs from the RTL author. Hosted certification (TM Forum, MEF/Iometrix, O-RAN OTIC) is an external attestation recorded as such, not a command. Everything configurable, small files, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged.

## P-knowledge-hub — Organisation knowledge hub: a shared, scoped, trust-labelled knowledge base across projects with its own protocol (DKP), layered under policy bundles, with a local mirror, offline outbox and promotion workflow

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/24 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-13: research and plan sharing information, databases, lessons, session context, decisions, rules, goals, policies, subagents, companions and configurations across projects of a company or division through a remote knowledge database with a custom protocol (propose it), beyond the centralized policy already planned; reuse the core; everything in the config file, CLI, MCP and prompts.

> Research note R-knowledge-hub (the research agent read the MCP, A2A, OCI, Electric, Nostr, Zep and Mem0 sources; several vendor features were snippets; Automerge, Matrix, Datomic and LangGraph store were not covered).
> Proposal DKP (ddflow.kb/1): immutable content-addressed records, separate signed attestations (approval, scan, endorse, still-true, disputed), sequence-numbered NDJSON feed with opaque cursors and up_to_date/must_refetch lines, signed snapshots, search with a token budget and provenance, propose-only agent tokens with the trust label set by the server, tombstones with reason classes (leak purges), a scope tree as the only ACL unit, bi-temporal fields with review_by.
> Layering and reuse: policy bundles (P-org-config: sources, layers, trust, lock, policy) stay the prescriptive channel and the only way to enforce; DKP is descriptive and advisory and lands in a separate local imported layer, never in project shards; precedence policy bundle > project operator records > org-endorsed > project-promoted > agent. The record contract (P-record-contract) gives history, change feed, RAG export and relevance context to every kind; the serve and auth work (P-remote) gives the hub's HTTP surface and tokens; trust fencing and the reviewer rule (D-reviewer-trust) give the injection defence; sessions and memory (P-agent-memory, P-context-sync) give the optional summary kind (default off); lessons promotion (P-lessons) and decision categories (P-decisions) give what is worth promoting; the extension seam (P-extension-seams) gives the transports as registry entries.
> NEW: the envelope and verbs, the client (mirror, outbox, sync), the publish pipeline (scan, quarantine, promotion), the git-mirror transport, a reference hub, and the layer in the fold.
> Rules: nothing from the hub ever carries a tool grant, hook or command (skills, subagents and companions arrive only through signed bundles); a failed sync is unavailable, never passed; the mirror serves stale reads with an as_of marker; secrets and personal data are scanned at publish; every setting is a knob in the file, CLI, MCP and prompts and every change is a logged event. Filed per D-usage-pacing-2026-10.

## P-autopilot — Autopilot: ddflow proposes, prepares and (within operator-set classes) executes project work, as architect and product manager, on an autonomy ladder with protected verifiers, budgets and a kill switch

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/18 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-13: research how ddflow can manage a project automatically: propose next features, optimise, correct old code, auto-develop software from user stories and goals; ddflow as architect of projects and manager of the architect workflow, and as product manager; best practices; what exists and is planned; the agent's and LLM's part.

> Research note R-autopilot (primary reads: Devin review, Darwin Gödel Machine, METR, Anthropic multi-agent, Böckeler; the rest snippets; OKRs, release trains, tech radar and debt registers not researched).
> Design: autonomy ladder per proposal class L0 suggest, L1 prepare, L2 execute with approval, L3 execute within budget; default L0; only the operator raises a class; a failed canary, reverted merge or skipped gate demotes it; direction, new dependencies with licence or security impact, public API and architecture changes are capped at L2. Loop: observe, assess, propose, approve, execute, verify, learn. Proposal types: feature, refactor, debt, bug sweep, doc fix, dependency upgrade, architecture change, each with an oracle and a stop rule. Architect workflow (context, drivers as quality attribute scenarios ranked by the operator, options with spikes, evaluation with a different-family reviewer and a red team, decision as an ADR, fitness functions as gates, scheduled re-evaluation) and product-manager workflow (outcome, opportunity tree, assumption tests, RICE with confidence penalty, now/next/later view derived from the queue, delivery as stories, release metrics, outcome review).
> Reuse (no second engine): proposals and person-only adoption and feature discovery (P-goals: B-prop-model, B-prop-discover), goals and progress (B-goal-model, B-goal-progress), typed observation proposals, retro, bounded experiments and effect measurement (P-observe), scheduled jobs and watches (P-schedule), decisions and ADR files and dependency policy (P-decisions), requirements, stories and product documents (P-product-docs), research workflows (P-research-flows), test workflows (P-test-flows), the governor and cost envelopes (P-governor, P-safeguards), spawn (P-spawn), lanes, metrics and spend (P-gaps), lessons promotion (P-lessons), the knowledge hub (P-knowledge-hub).
> NEW: the autonomy class table and demotion logic, the protected-verifier rule, fitness-function records and gates, the architect and product workflows as template data, the calibration record, the kill switch, and the observation jobs not yet planned (debt and drift sweeps).
> Rules: the agent never edits its oracle, the gate configuration, review prompts or cost limits; a proposal without evidence is rejected by the tool; ceremony scales with risk; open proposals per operator are capped; the discovery job that reads the web has no write access beyond its proposal and executors never read raw web content. Everything configurable, small files, CLI+MCP+prompt, logged. Filed per D-usage-pacing-2026-10.

## P-constellation — Constellation: sister projects sharing specs (OpenAPI, protobuf, ASN.1, YANG, DBC, register maps), libraries, requirements and ICDs, with owners, consumers, breaking-change gates, change requests, baselines and onboarding

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/45 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-13: how ddflow manages collaboration between sister projects (shared libraries, API specifications for API-driven development, test specifications, requirements, user stories, specifications, ICDs); best practices and other tools; how to manage OpenAPI, ASN.1 and other spec types; how to onboard projects with such specifications and documents; extend what exists and is planned, reuse the cores, add tasks for gaps.

> Research note R-constellation (Pact, oasdiff, buf, Confluent, Apicurio, Backstage, Avro canonical form and YANG rules fetched; ASN.1, DBC, IP-XACT, ICD and change-board practice partly snippets or unverified). Today nothing in the queue covers more than one project: only the org bundle fetcher, co-change checks, the multi-clone work and the hub and test-pin phases filed this session.
> Design: a constellation manifest lists member projects (name, remote, role, trust); a spec is a record with owner, consumers, declared version, a model digest (canonical parsed form) next to the content digest, a named checker and compatibility level, a lifecycle and a source; references across projects are project:id@digest; breaking classification comes from a checker run, never an agent's opinion; consumers are edges with an impact query; a compatibility matrix of test results with SUT pins feeds a can-i-release gate; owners raise change requests with per-consumer state, waivers and a deprecation window; baselines freeze sets of spec versions and need a human approval (the ICD cut); a sibling project is mirrored read-only, trust=imported, and events reference sibling events by digest, never embed them; imported spec text is untrusted and scanned.
> Reuse (no second engine): data-declared record kinds, the workflow-template engine, packs, approvals, waivers, sensitivity, event registry, MCP budget and evaluation harness (P-shared-engines); test results, pins and verdicts (P-test-flows, P-test-domains); requirement baselines and suspect links (P-product-docs); the org git fetcher and bundle format (P-org-config); the hub mirror and sinks (P-knowledge-hub, P-control-planes); scheduled jobs (P-schedule); document types (P-docs-generic).
> NEW: the manifest, the spec kind and six format-adapter groups, digest pinning across projects, consumer edges, the breaking-change gate, the matrix and gate, change requests, the sibling mirror, the library registry, the onboarding workflow and drift audit.
> Rules: a non-owner never edits a spec, it becomes a change request; pins are by digest; sibling content is data, not instructions; a missing checker is unavailable, never passed; nothing here sends, signs or spends (D-product-docs-r3). Filed per D-usage-pacing-2026-10.

## B-hot-files — Fewer shared hot files: split the files every task edits so independent work stops sharing a lease

`done` · ██████████████████ 6/6 tasks · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Operator 2026-10-02 (research R-task-time): the biggest serial resources are held ~44 minutes per lease: mcp.py (743 min over 17 leases), cli.py (535/12), config.py (484/11), api/lifecycle.py (452/13), core/model.py (422/9). Splitting each along its existing seam means independent tasks touch different files. All splits are behaviour-neutral (re-export, tests unchanged) and must land in a quiet window: each one blocks every other task that touches the file, so claim late, merge fast, and sequence them (B-split-mcp-tools first, it is already queued). Plus the lease policy idea: hold hot-file leases only for edit and merge (B-lease-edit-only-hold).

## B-upstream-reporting — Upstream bug reports: sanitized, deduplicated, operator-consented, with an optional fix patch

`open` · ████████░░░░░░░░░░ 6/14 tasks · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Operator 2026-10-02, verbatim: "Add a feature to ddflow if in principle the ddflow or the agent itself find or suspect a bug in ddflow, to propose to the operator/user to automatically fill it up to github or even propose a fix and fill up the bugfix in github or if you have access directly to the ddflow code"

> Research (2026-10-02, R-upstream-reporting): 249 bug.found events in this log (median 416 chars) carry only item+summary; the 21 cross-project reports (home-simulator) had a REPRO block 21/21 but no ddflow version, install source, commit, python/os, session or traceback 0/21, and the item field empty 21/21. No ddflow message anywhere tells an agent to report a ddflow defect upstream (onboard.md:92 files them into the MANAGED project's own log). Hand classification of the 249: mechanical-at-failure detectors (traceback, remedy naming a missing command, version-skew refusal, refusal-reported-as-success) would have caught ~9%; offline-mechanical (tests/CI) ~15%; ~75% needed an agent's or person's judgement - the agent is the primary source. Redaction corpus: private IPv4 in 22 events, /home/<user> in 759 events, project names in 47 bug summaries; bug text is not redacted today (sessions.redact covers session prompt/note and secrets only). A prefilled issue URL fits every real report (median 1.5 KB, max 3 KB with environment block; limit ~8 KB). gh, glab, tokens and ssh keys are absent on this machine; upstream delian/ddflow-mcp has 0 issues. forge.py already separates ForgeUnavailable from ForgeError. Install source/commit are derivable from PEP 610 direct_url.json (adopt.py already reads it privately).

> Decision D-upstream-reporting (accepted). Order: 1,2 -> 3 -> {4,5,6} -> consent -> 7 -> 8 -> {9,10,11} -> 12 -> 13. Tasks 1-5 add only new files and can start now; later ones touch hot files (cli.py, mcp.py, config.py, api/knowledge.py, api/reporting.py).

## B-viewers — Viewers: list and show for tasks, phases, bugs, research, sessions and the log, on CLI and MCP

`open` · ███████████████░░░ 6/7 tasks · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Operator 2026-10-02: 'What about dedicated session, bug, phase, log, tasks, research viewers?' -> 'Yes'. Today only decisions have list/show/search; task/phase/bug/research are add-only, sessions are readable only through `export sessions`, and `show <id>` is the single generic detail view. Model the new viewers on `decision list|show|search`. Shared filters: --state, --phase, --tag, --agent, --since, --limit, --json. MCP: ONE consolidated read tool (ddflow_list kind=task|phase|bug|research|session) rather than six, because tools/list is at its byte budget (tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py); sits in the standard tier. Every output goes through the existing redaction/provenance and payload bounds (surfaces/mcp_bound.py). Each task updates README (D-readme-current). Order: 1 -> {2,3,4} -> 5 -> 6.

> Operator 2026-10-01, verbatim: "Add a feature development to ask agent to check if a bug, or feature for development, task, phase or whatever it adds, is not duplicated and if it is, to preferably update and extend the current content if it is not closed (in case of closed, or working on it - log a new bug, task, whatever, to not lose the changes) so the fix of the other bug to cover the new informantion of there is any. The idea is that we want to prevent duplication as much as possible (check if ddflow can by itself without llm - do a research for it maybe with nltk or other tools do a fuzzy search and ask the user in case of cli or agent to double check if the new data duplicates or extends pre existing one)? Add this as new phase for development with tasks after you do extensive research and propose a plan"

> Research (2026-10-01, research R-dedupe-matchers): on 40 verified duplicate pairs, 17 related and 18 hard negatives from ddflow's own log, a stdlib TF-IDF cosine (code-aware tokenizer, ~10-line suffix stemmer, ids/shas masked) reranking FTS5 top-50 candidates puts the existing record in the top 3 for 95% (top 5 97.5%), finds the open task that fixes a new bug in the top 3 for 95%, at 2.5 ms median / 5.2 ms p95 per add on run_nemo_run's 6,100 records. NLTK, rapidfuzz, difflib, MinHash and scikit-learn were all no better or worse. A score cannot separate a duplicate from a different bug in the same function (hard negatives 0.43-0.64 sit inside the duplicate band), so ddflow shows candidates and the adding agent or operator answers. Benchmark scripts: the parent session's scratchpad dedup/ (corpus.py, labels.py, matchers.py, bench.py).

> Decision D-no-duplicates (accepted). Task order: 1 -> 2 -> {3, 4 after B168} -> 5 -> {6, 7, 8, 9, 10} -> 11. Several tasks touch files bug-fix agents hold on 2026-10-01 (cli.py, mcp.py, api/knowledge.py, api/lifecycle.py, api/items.py, api/reporting.py, config.py): claim after those merge.

## BL-shared-log — The in-repo event log: clone-and-continue, and safe merges across users and agents

## P-accrete-fit — Accrete fit: ideas from a context-graph/knowledge-engine vendor and the generic seams (why-corpus export, egress-checked consult, recall probe, memory consolidation) that make any such service easy to connect

`open` · ████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/9 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-21 (verbatim): "Check this tool - https://www.accrete.ai/why-accrete and research it and see if there are ideas we can pick up for ddflow to implement, as well as separately, would ddflow be easy to integrate with accrete and give me opinion, phase + tasks for the gaps, with proper dependencies and wave to implement"

> Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/accrete.md (task ACF-research) and research notes R-accrete-*.

> VERDICT IN ONE PARAGRAPH: Accrete (accrete.ai) is a closed, sales-led enterprise 'context graph / Knowledge Engine' vendor (plus a US-government product, Argus). It publishes NO public API, SDK, MCP spec or webhook docs (REPORTED by a third-party catalog and confirmed by the absence on every page read), so an Accrete-specific adapter cannot be specified or tested today. Almost every idea it sells (decision rationale, provenance, confidence, temporal validity, permissioned knowledge, memory consolidation, citations) is already planned in ddflow (P-lessons, P-decisions, P-agent-memory, P-knowledge-hub, P-requirements, P-observe) and D-graph-scope-r1 explicitly declines a knowledge-graph memory. This phase therefore adds ONLY the gaps: a read-only 'why corpus' export an external consumer can ingest, an egress-checked consult of an external knowledge source, a recall probe built from the project's own history, and propose-only memory consolidation, plus decision, vendor verification, end-to-end and docs tasks. No Accrete-specific code is built until Accrete gives access (ACF-verify) and the operator says so (ACF-decide).

> WAVES: W1 ACF-research -> ACF-decide. W2 (parallel, disjoint globs) ACF-why-export, ACF-consult-out, ACF-recall-probe, ACF-memory-consolidate, ACF-verify. W3 ACF-e2e. W4 ACF-docs. Held behind the P-gaps core/docs wave per D-old-work-behind-core-docs (phase needs).

> LINKED, NOT RE-ADDED (already planned): decision traces/ruled-out log = D-reasoning-log + B-am-capture + B-dec-model; per-record provenance/validity/confidence = KB-envelope, KB-attest, B-security-provenance; permissioning = KB-scope, KB-auth, SE-sensitivity; outcome feedback = P-lessons.recurrence, P-lessons.effect, P-observe.effect; staleness = PL-staleness, B-dec-review; citations = RQM-reviewer, RQM-ack; inbound remote knowledge/MCP = RQM-sources, RQM-mcp-client, KB-mirror; ddflow as MCP server for another agent platform = P-control-planes (MCP profiles, scoped tokens), P-remote.serve; outbound notification webhooks = CP-notify-sinks; platform tool guard = PM-descriptor, PM-guard.

## P-agent-rules — Coexist with a project's own agent rules and slash commands, whichever agents and IDEs it already uses

`open` · ███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/12 tasks · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> A project that adopts ddflow usually already has instructions of its own: always-loaded or path-scoped rule files, slash-command files, a todo file, a lessons file, an issue tracker it treats as the log. Today ddflow neither reads nor accounts for them, so (a) a rule written for one agent never reaches the others working in the same repository, (b) the project's commands exist in one IDE only, (c) path-triggered policies ('touch X, then check Y') can only be encoded as gates that are always on or skipped by hand, and (d) the project's own history imports lossily. This phase makes ddflow read, report and bridge those surfaces for any project and any agent. Out of scope, deliberately: rewriting a project's rules. Where they conflict with ddflow's workflow (a second source of truth for the queue, a different branch lifecycle, several always-loaded rules with no precedence between them) ddflow REPORTS the conflict and the operator resolves it.
