## P-coherence — Knowledge coherence: every add is checked for duplicates, upgrades and contradictions, and someone decides

`open` · ████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/5 tasks · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Builds on D-no-duplicates (add-time duplicate check). Adds: coverage of every record kind (bug, lesson, decision, rule, instruction, prompt template, memory, task, phase); a closed match whose work is not done is re-added, linked to it; detection of contradiction and upgrade against active records; a decision step (agent for tasks, bugs, lessons; operator for decisions, rules, instructions) choosing keep / extend / coordinate / supersede / delete; nothing is ever erased from the log.

## P-commit-messages — Commit message management: contexts, layered templates, lint, signing and push policy, as config and existing tool families

`open` · ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/23 tasks · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Operator 2026-10-22 (verbatim): "Separately - can you make a research and create capabilities how ddflow can orchestrate, configure and manage the git commit messages - for example, if a company has a standard, or a project wants to follow a standard how the commit message is formatted, and what it contains? Can you investigate best practices, ability to sign commit messages, push, pre-commit rules, what we could extend and support as templates (aka jinja templates) and manage text with the agent/llm, but also allow the project, user, company policies, and default templates for comments? Can you make sure such commit message management supports config files, templates, editing via cli, potential mcp tool (extend the expected family of tools with options, not adding brand new tool, as we'd like to keep the amount of mcp tools small to support agents that cannot have large amount of tools), and user to manage, review, edit, delete, change, etc via prompt? If there might be different contexts of commit messages, we might need to be able to support different templates, so think of context, templates, but also how this could be extended by the user depending on the workflow or the project or the company policies". Research: docs/ddflow/research/commit-messages.md. Proposals (operator decides): docs/ddflow/decisions/commit-messages.md. Held behind the P-gaps core and the docs wave (D-old-work-behind-core-docs-accepted: phase needs P-docs-generic, P-roadmap, P-docs-search; the P-gaps core is done). Related: P-requirements, P-id-consistency, P-agent-lifecycle (hook manifest), P-org-config, P-config-engine, P-tool-diet. No new MCP tool.

## P-completion — Shell completion: commands, options, values and IDs for bash, zsh and fish

`open` · ████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/9 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Research R-shell-completion-design; D-completion-scope (bash+zsh+fish, argcomplete optional extra, IDs from the sqlite index, offered at onboard/adopt). GENERIC BY CONSTRUCTION (operator 2026-10-29): a new command, option, choice, record kind or harness must be completed with ZERO completion code. Rules: (1) one source of truth: the argparse parser that build_parser() returns (declarative registry Params + the ~43 hand-written add_argument calls); the completion engine introspects it at TAB time and no command, option or choice is listed anywhere else; (2) the three shell scripts contain no command names; (3) value kinds (record ids, phases, gates, agents, paths) come from metadata on the argument (Param.complete, inferred by default from the argument's name and the RecordKind registry) so a new record kind or id-like argument is picked up automatically, and an argument that should not complete must say so in an explicit exemption list; (4) ratchet tests fail the build when a new argument cannot be completed or is silently skipped. Argcomplete starts ddflow per TAB (about 1 s), so COMP-ids-fast keeps that path import-light.

## P-dsh-fit — DeepSeek Harness (dsh) fit: dsh as a supported harness (descriptor first, cordis overlay, hooks bridge), as a lane worker (headless --json, ACP), and what it exposes

`open` · ████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 5/21 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-22 (verbatim): "Investigate dsh - deepseek harness (https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) and see how we could use it as an agent, how we can integrate with it, or integrate ddflow to be with, by dsh and add it to the supported list of coding agents we have"

> Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/dsh.md (task DSH-research), source read at deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness commit 687f282 (v0.2.1-rc.2); nothing was executed.

> VERDICT: dsh (npm @deepseek-ai/dsh, MIT, DeepSeek AI, developer preview, TypeScript on Cordis, Node >=22.19) is a real, general coding-agent harness: web UI, headless one-shot (--json), SDK JSON-RPC, and an ACP stdio server. It is NOT tied to DeepSeek models (pi-ai providers, OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic custom endpoints). It reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md natively, .agents/skills, a built-in MCP client (stdio and streamable HTTP, tools list_changed honoured, no elicitation or prompts), and has OPT-IN experimental bridges that run existing Claude Code and Codex hooks.json command hooks. TRAPS: MCP servers and hooks are configured only through Cordis YAML patch layers (profile, home, or --patch), never a project file; hooks bridges are not in any shipped bundle; stdio MCP children get a scrubbed env (KEY/PASSWORD/SECRET/TOKEN and all DSH_* dropped); headless approval has no answerer (ask resolves unavailable, fail closed) unless DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access; instruction budget 64 KiB; hook transcript_path is always empty; SessionStart hooks run detached.

> ALREADY PLANNED, LINKED NOT RE-ADDED: descriptors = P-agent-parity.new-descriptors and descriptor-v2; lane launcher = P-agent-parity.launcher; ACP = P-acp (AC-*); verify/manifest = P-agent-lifecycle; profiles = MTD-profiles; client table = SU-client-table; transcript import = B-am-ingest; lean start = P-lean-start.

> WAVES: see the verified line appended after the tasks were filed.

> WAVES (as built, verified acyclic with all needs existing and the in-phase DSH needs resolved): 1 DSH-research (done, free); 2 DSH-facts, DSH-mcp-shape, DSH-client-row, DSH-decide (carries the P-gaps core/docs hold); 3 DSH-descriptor (dsh joins the supported list), DSH-session-ingest; 4 DSH-fixtures, DSH-overlay; 5 DSH-hooks, DSH-mcp-profile, DSH-onboard-verify, DSH-lane, DSH-bundle (optional); 6 DSH-lane-acp; 7 DSH-e2e; 8 DSH-docs. ## P-goals — Goals, principles and proposals on the guidance engine: defeasible principles with recorded deviations, measurable goals injected into the brief, and periodic feature discovery that proposes and never queues

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/15 tasks · 2 abandoned · needs `P-decisions`, `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`, `P-record-contract`

> Operator 2026-10-11 (verbatim, also recorded as a session prompt): "Separately, Is there a way for a workflow management engine to follow project goals (have the concept of goals) and automatically research periodically what next features might be needed and suggest that, while separately follow common principles for the project which are some sort of a weak rule, which defines what we prefer to do unless there is a better reason, and then we have a set of strict or unstrict as defined rules, which have to be followed? ... propose features or fill-up gaps, investigate if for those features we could use the already existing internals and rules + decisions + architectural decisions engines implemented or planned to be implemented and add a phase + tasks for us to do them."

> Evidence: R-goals-existing-map (CONFIRMED: what exists and what the attached document got wrong) and R-goals-principles-proposals-design (THEORETICAL: survey of Kiro, Spec Kit, Claude Code, Cursor, Gatekeeper, Kyverno, Dependabot, Renovate, Jules, Linear, SonarQube, ArchUnit, MADR, RFC 2119, and the design).

> DESIGN IN ONE PARAGRAPH (nothing here is a parallel store):
> - RULES (strict or unstrict) are the guidance engine's rule and decision records: enforcement block | warn | advisory, checks, waivers, review_by. Already built in services/guidance; P-decisions finishes and wires them. This phase adds nothing to what a rule IS.
> - PRINCIPLES are NOT a new kind. A principle is a guidance record (a decision or a rule) whose OVERRIDE MODE is deviate: follow it unless you record a reason. A rule is override=waive (a person approves, scoped, at most 90 days, D-decision-management) or none (an org floor). RFC 2119 vocabulary: MUST = block + waive|none, SHOULD = warn + deviate, MAY = advisory. A finding against a SHOULD must be answered (comply or deviate with a reason) before the item completes; repeated deviations flag the principle for review. That feedback loop is what keeps a soft rule from silently vanishing or silently becoming hard.
> - GOALS are a new definition-record kind (def.* events, record surface, search, history, upcasters come free): a title, an owner, a status, linked phases/tasks/decisions, and key results with a measurable source (dag progress, a ddflow metric, an approved check command, or a dated manual attestation that goes stale). Progress is computed, never typed. A goal never overrides a rule; it steers what the brief shows, what discovery proposes and what the roadmap displays.
> - PROPOSALS (periodic feature discovery) are a second new def-record kind that lives OUTSIDE the queue until a person adopts it, so next/claim never see an unreviewed idea. A shipped, opt-in schedule job files ONE research item per run whose output is at most K proposals, each citing a goal, evidence, a principle check, a size estimate and a dedupe result against the board AND against rejected proposals. Adopt/defer/reject (with reason) are person-only. Caps, backpressure, a circuit breaker and a rejected-ideas memory prevent idea spam.
> - PRECEDENCE: org floor > project rule (block) > accepted decision > principle > preference; the nearest scope wins within a tier; goals never constrain.

> Order: decide -> {deviation, cites, goal model} -> {progress, proposal model} -> {inject, discover} -> report -> acceptance -> eval. Held behind the P-gaps core, the docs wave and P-decisions (D-old-work-behind-core-docs): it builds on the decision engine tasks B-dec-model, B-dec-waivers, B-dec-monitor, B-dec-review, on B-research-items and the schedule tasks, and on B-gap-metrics.

> Extends (does not duplicate): B-dec-model, B-dec-waivers, B-dec-review, B-rules-onto-record-surface, B-rm-template, B-research-items, B-sched-defaults, B-sched-escalation, B-gap-metrics, B-org-kinds, B-org-policy (each got a marked paragraph on 2026-10-11).

> Record-surface contract extension 2026-10-11 (operator request: "make sure all goals and principles and rules follow the principles of the current project - mcp and cli interfaces, add, edit, delete, modify, merge, split, search, context insert, rag export ... sessions are automatically informed for changes, they retrieve brief on session start, and can also search, ask, or automatically receive context ..."; decision D-record-surface-contract, rows RC1-RC12). Goals, principles (guidance records with override=deviate), rules, decisions, proposals, waivers and deviations are record kinds under that contract. The shared mechanisms are built ONCE in phase P-record-contract (B-rc-lifecycle: history, supersede, merge, split, restore, ack; B-rc-participation: search, recall and resources derived from the descriptor; B-rc-changes: the change feed and its doors, so running sessions are told of changes; B-rc-context: relevance-matched automatic context and `recall --for`; B-rc-rag-export; B-rc-conformance: a generated test). This phase therefore waits for P-record-contract, and its tasks declare descriptors and registrations rather than writing per-kind search sources, resources, injectors, lifecycle code or notification lines. B-goal-acceptance gains the scripted conformance scenario (item 9). Extended tasks: B-goal-decide (Q12-14), B-goal-model, B-goal-deviation, B-goal-progress, B-goal-inject, B-prop-model, B-goal-acceptance.

## P-id-consistency — Id consistency: ids minted by different agents for one project follow one convention (allocation, conformance, phase prefixes, templates, vocabulary presets)

`open` · ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/8 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-22 (verbatim): "The goal is to keep consistency between ID generated by different agents for the same project". Operator answered "Yes, create P-id-consistency (Recommended)": one phase with waves: allocation test and conformance lint first, then phase prefixes and templates for new kinds, then vocabulary aliases and presets; held behind the org layer where it needs it.

> EVIDENCE (measured on this project's log, see the conformance-lint task): 836 bugs, of which 677 carry the machine form B<hash> and 159 are agent-chosen slugs (B-ci-gate-prints-passed-with-failing-tests...); 464 fix tasks, of which 385 are fix-B<hash> and 79 are fix-B-<slug>; task ids use dozens of ad-hoc prefixes (US-, RQM-, SPEC-, PI-, ACF-, LS-, SU-, B-uni, P-agent..., fix-B...). Cause: --id / caller-named ids let every agent invent a shape.

> GOVERNING RECORDS: decision D-id-schemes-final (templates per kind defaulting to today's ids, {seq} keys, one namespace with a taken-key check, vocabulary aliases); research Rb1695227af; built already: B-id-config ([ids] templates), B-id-generator (id service). Org-wide conventions arrive through B-org-layers.

> WAVES: 1 allocation proof + conformance lint (and ID-decide, the operator questions); 2 phase prefix registry, templates for new kinds, templates for tasks/phases; 3 vocabulary aliases and presets (needs B-org-layers), end-to-end transcript test; 4 docs.

Stage 1 (MVP, priority 50): LC-decide -> LC-wake -> LC-release (release-at-enqueue on the existing merge queue) -> LC-reuse -> LC-e2e; needs no P-batch-gates task. Reuse: services/waits.py, DX-watch-job resume tokens, DX-park-and-resume, SW-seed-pack/CC-resume-pack formats, SW-pull, services/bisect ddmin. ## P-lock-lifecycle — Lock lifecycle: lock a file only when it is first written, release or downgrade during gates and reviews, notify others of merges and in-flight work, hand small changes to the owner, so long locks stop blocking parallel agents

`open` · ███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 13/73 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-11-02: break the long locks together with the DAG optimizer, granular test runs and merged gates/reviews; lock files individually only just before modification and unlock them for others during the long gate and review waits; notify others of changes before the merge to main; let others work on an owned file optimistically and send their small changes to the owner who integrates and passes the gates; use git merges, cherry-picks, messages and notifications. Evidence: R-lock-inventory (hold time median 65 min, 45 percent in gates and reviews, 21 percent after the last commit, release-at-enqueue never used), R-lock-landscape and R-lock-landscape-verified (outside), R-handoff-protocol (experiments with cherry-pick, format-patch, hidden refs, bundle, merge-tree, patch-id). This phase MERGES the earlier unbuilt lock, wait, drift and sync tasks so all can run together: they were moved here from P-lane-consolidation, bugs-2, P-change-surface and the DX-* group. Supersedes the 'early release while only reviews run' rejection in D-lease-hold-limit-r2 (new decision filed with the phase).

## P-multiuser — Several users, several clones, several agents, several ddflow versions: detect, prevent and explain cross-clone problems (git-native, no server)

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/12 tasks · 1 abandoned · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Operator request 2026-10-11 (verbatim): "Do a research of what this tool does or is expected to do (future task for implementing) and what issues and problems could happen if multiple users work on the same project and have their own local git clone of it use local ddflow tools some potentially with different versions and do decisions in parallel and work and merge the code periodically (no matter what branching flow approach it is selected by the developers to work with) - how ddflow would behave and support such multi user work, what issues could or might happen, how could we prevent or mitigate them and respectively what features we need to develop in ddflow to make it more rebust for multi user multi agent multi version use?"
> Evidence: R-multiuser-experiments (CONFIRMED, 12 scenario families run on real git with three ddflow versions; scripts in the research coordinator's scratchpad mu/ directory, copied into tests/ by B-mu-harness) and R-multiuser-survey (THEORETICAL). Bugs filed from it: B230e852e10 and B36aa4c8ee5 (BROKEN, their fix tasks run unheld), B2809f4213b, B71dedb76d2, B0dcccd8594, B90b43dd2d8, B5a6651cd8e, B839f599cb5, B6b8d1f7a0f, B63635ddc6a, Ba24a8d32ee, Bec9a971c5d, B924bdc92d7 (DEGRADED, fixed by the tasks below). Existing multi-user work reused, not repeated: B190/B205 (clone-unique derived ids), B191 (contested ids and claims), B192 ([flow].claims=remote), B193 (docs/ddflow/MULTI-USER.md), B-hy-commit-events and B189 (committing the shards), B-gap-log-backup, B-gap-log-scale, B-org-* (central config), B-coh-* (contradictions), B-res-* (resume). No server, no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon): everything is git-native. Held behind the P-gaps core and the docs wave like the other old work (D-old-work-behind-core-docs); the two BROKEN bug fixes are not held. MUST = needed for several users each with several agents; GREAT = worth building; the SKIP list is in B-mu-decide.

## P-optimizer — Optimizer: one swappable scheduling port, affinity and aversion preferences, conflict-aware lane placement, measured by replay

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/32 tasks

> Research R-affinity-scheduling. Reduce lease waits, merge conflicts and duplicated work by ordering, not by new locks. Builds on SW-score (done), SW-pull, DX-lease-real-overlap, ETA-simulate, the similarity matcher and MV-path-moves. CONFORMANCE (r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-everything-configurable, D-universal-principles, D-adapters-answers): every weight, cap and threshold is a knob (file, CLI, MCP, prompt); deterministic (integer scores, total tie-break by id, no wall-clock, no hash-order, no randomness) and explainable (every placement carries its itemised terms); affinity and aversion are PREFERENCES that reorder, never filters: hard constraints stay needs and globs; the default behaviour is unchanged until the operator switches the optimizer; no model call needed; HELD until the manual git refactor ends. Research R-affinity-scheduling.

## P-perf-metrics — Performance metrics: measure tools, tests, LLM waits, agents and resources, report with statistics and graphs, and propose optimizations on a schedule so effort per feature stays flat as the code and test suite grow

`open` · ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 4/44 tasks

> Operator 2026-11-02: collect performance metrics (time per tool and gate, cpu, network, disk, io, waits on LLMs, which agents and models do well or badly, bugs generated, tool calls) and analyse them periodically in a scheduled job that proposes optimizations to the user, to ddflow and to the workflow, so a small feature does not cost exponentially more as the codebase and the unit tests grow. Reports with statistics and graphs on request. Research: R-perf-landscape (outside), R-perf-inventory (inside). EXTENDS, does not duplicate: services/metrics (facts, summary, forecast, retro), core/flowsignals, infra/signals + flow.sample tick, services/flakes, services/cmdrunner + gates/runner evidence (elapsed_s, waited_s), COUNT_PASSES in services/schedule, P-observe (telemetry, detectors, findings, proposals), B-perf-bench (ddflow own commands), B-gap-spend (usage ledger), B-sub-metrics (agent stats), SCH-review-inbox, P-eta, OPT-history. ## P-pidev-fit — Pi (pi.dev) fit: Pi as a supported harness (extension, MCP exposure, trust), as a lane worker over RPC/JSON, session ingest, and the generic gaps it exposes

`open` · ███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/13 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-21 (verbatim): "Check for the same (as accrete) - pi.dev - research and see if it overlaps with ddflow, are there features we could pick on, and separately could we integrate with it"

> Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/pi-dev.md (task PI-research) and research notes R-pidev-*.

> VERDICT: Pi (pi.dev, github.com/earendil-works/pi, MIT, Earendil Inc.) is a minimal terminal coding-agent harness: a HARNESS ddflow should support, not a competitor and not a workflow tool (it deliberately ships no sub-agents, plan mode, permission popups, todos). It has a real TypeScript extension API (tool_call can block, agent_before_settle can continue, session_before_compact, input, session_start/shutdown), a built-in MCP client (stdio and streamable HTTP, list_changed honoured), print/JSON/RPC/SDK modes, reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Integration as a harness is MODERATE (extension template + descriptor + normalizer); as a lane worker over RPC EASY-TO-MODERATE; Pi consuming ddflow records needs nothing new (it reads the same instruction files and skills).

> TRAPS found: (1) Pi MCP servers default to `codemode` exposure: ddflow's tools are NOT declared to the model unless the entry says `exposure: direct` (or `toolExposure`). (2) `.pi/extensions` and `.pi/mcp.json` load only after project trust; print/JSON/RPC modes silently skip them unless `--approve` or a saved decision, so a headless lane would have no ddflow. (3) `pi.exec` has no stdin option: hook payload to `ddflow hooks run` needs node:child_process. (4) Pi asks for no approval before tool calls; containment is ddflow's. (5) install telemetry defaults on.

> ALREADY PLANNED, LINKED NOT RE-ADDED: pi descriptor = P-agent-parity.new-descriptors; stop-to-continue for Pi's plugin = P-agent-parity.continuation; plugin hook writer = P-agent-parity.kilo-plugin; lane launcher = P-agent-parity.launcher; ACP client/backend = P-acp; transcript import = B-am-ingest; per-client MCP profiles = MTD-profiles; per-client list_changed table = SU-client-table; docs-lift A/B = B-skills-adherence-eval.

> WAVES: W1 PI-research (free, docs only) -> PI-decide (carries the P-gaps core/docs hold of D-old-work-behind-core-docs; everything below waits behind it). W2 (parallel, disjoint globs) PI-facts, PI-normalizer, PI-client-row, PI-session-ingest. W3 PI-extension, PI-exposure-map, PI-onboard-verify, PI-lane-rpc. W4 PI-lane-events. W5 PI-e2e. W6 PI-docs.

> WAVES (as built, verified acyclic with all needs existing): 1 PI-research (free, docs only); 2 PI-decide (carries the hold), PI-client-row; 3 PI-facts, PI-session-ingest; 4 PI-normalizer, PI-exposure-map, PI-onboard-verify, PI-lane-rpc; 5 PI-extension, PI-lane-events; 6 PI-e2e; 7 PI-docs. ## P-requirements — Engineering requirements and standards: a scoped, layered, verifiable requirement record that reaches agents contextually and periodically, with compliance evidence

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/27 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-21 (verbatim): "can you check if we can manage project requirements (as the rest of the documents, both as documentation, but also both as ability to insert the requirements brief in the sessions and contextually where applicable, with the respective check in the agent sessions, the same as managing rules, policies, goals, exposing requirements to the user to manage with all the abilities to edit, delete, list, duplication checks, etc) - as for example to manage requirements of how the software to build - aka use cmake, conan, this type of format of cmake, etc. Such requirements and standards should be possible to be checked and received both from external tools (codeguide-mcp or other mcp servers), corporate policies (remote, local), or per project requirements, user managed imposed, or stored as requirements doc files, managed by ddflow. Check if we have these features, or we plan to implement them, what of the internal cores we could reuse, how to make the rules, requirements, goal, policies, documentation, skills, subagents, etc - to be instructing periodically the agent sessions, are we having gaps, how to improve on that. Do a deep research, and propose phase + tasks for corrections if any"

> Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/requirements-management.md (task RQM-research) and the research notes R-req-* recorded 2026-10-21.

> WHAT THIS PHASE IS: ENGINEERING requirements and standards (how the software is built: CMake >= 3.25, Conan 2 for dependencies, CMakePresets, no in-source builds, compiler flags, language style, licensing, security, branching/PR, test and documentation policy), as one scoped, layered, verifiable record that reaches agents contextually and periodically and leaves compliance evidence. It is NOT the product-requirements pipeline of P-product-docs (EARS text, stakeholders, baselines, RFP packs); both use the SAME shipped record kind, ddflow/templates/kinds/requirement.toml, which already exists (lifecycle proposed..verified, source, stakeholders) but is inert: no scoping, no strength, no verification, no injection (RecordKind.applies is declared and unused, api/records.py; guidance inject.collect returns rules and decisions only, services/guidance/inject.py:104). RQM-model extends the descriptor with a `class` field (product | constraint | standard | policy); PD-req-kind adds its EARS/baseline fields on top of the same descriptor. Do not build a second engine.

> REUSE (confirmed in code): record surface (CRUD, search, recall, resources, history, supersede, merge, split: B-rc-lifecycle/participation done); data kinds (SE-kind-data done); guidance engine scoping, ranking, budget, provenance fence, similarity dedupe (services/guidance); checks and waivers modules (built, tested, UNWIRED: no caller outside services/guidance); doc types and B-dt-rules guidance-per-document; the cadenced footer (config_sections/reinstruct.py, services/obligations.py); agent brief (services/agent_brief.py); companions registry; org layers (P-org-config) for corporate sources.

> SEQUENCING: the first tasks depend only on done work. Doors that need the open record-contract tasks (RQM-doors needs B-rc-context and B-rc-changes), org layers (RQM-layers needs B-org-layers, B-org-sources, B-org-trust), the pipeline field (RQM-gate needs B-pipe-model) and the strength/override model (RQM-strength needs B-goal-deviation) are explicitly gated on them; nothing here re-implements those. Held behind the P-gaps core/docs wave like P-goals per D-old-work-behind-core-docs unless the operator lifts it.

## P-research — Research as a verified, maintained workflow: invoked on every research request, claims with sources and validity, independent verification, injected where relevant, revisable with history, editable by the operator

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/28 tasks · 4 abandoned · needs `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Builds on P-coherence (duplicates and contradictions across kinds), BL-knowledge (B199 edit/retire, B204 recall-first, B196/B201 views), B-research-items (research as DAG items whose verdict files tasks, research at the start of a phase) and B-semantic-recall. Principles: recall before research; every claim has a source and a grade; a different model family verifies; nothing is deleted, only superseded or invalidated with a reason (Zep/Mem0g); stale knowledge is labelled and re-verified; the operator is asked when verification fails or research contradicts a decision.

## P-resume — Crash-resilient continuation: a restarted agent picks up where the last one stopped, automatically when provably safe, by asking when not

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/5 tasks · 4 abandoned

> Research R7edf8f33f7. Principle: every multi-step action leaves a trace that says what was intended and what finished; a restart reads the trace, proves what is dead, and either continues (safe) or asks the operator one clear question (ambiguous). Nothing is ever discarded: salvage first.

> D-recovery-one-design (2026-10-23): D-orphan-recovery governs; B-res-resume, B-res-brief-recovery-link, B-res-heartbeat and B-res-inflight-gates folded into the DX-recovery tasks; close this phase when the kept B-res-* tasks are done.

## P-schedule — Scheduled and event-triggered jobs: recurring audits, CI parity, and automatic remediation

`open` · ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 4/31 tasks · 1 abandoned

> Operator 2026-10-04, after a pre-push failure: ddflow should run scheduled jobs (weekly unit+integration tests and bug fixing, weekly whole-codebase bug audit incl. algorithmic bugs, documentation correctness, architecture/optimisation/library review, security, dependency upgrades, usability/robustness/requirements 'fill checks', periodic pre-commit/CI health) and event-triggered jobs (crash, bug deviation, pre-commit fail, repeated bugs) for this or any project, managed like everything else (CLI, MCP tool and prompts, list/edit/search, agent can improve, dedupe, conflict check, dependencies between jobs), defaults shipped as overridable templates. Research R0c36d18a08 (why push fails), R83ac363816 (schedulers), R0f97f9d716 (triggers); decisions D-sched-no-daemon, D-sched-triggers-separate, D-trigger-actions-create-items, D-ci-parity. FIRST VALUE: the ci gate and the post-merge main check (tasks B-ci-*) stop the push failures. Overlaps already queued and to be folded in, not duplicated: B-precommit-integration (the standards gate runs pre-commit; B-ci-gate builds on it), B-doctor-overdue-cadences (absorbed by B-sched-due), B-security-pass, B-architecture-pass, B-dependency-upgrades, B-dupes-sweep (become shipped default jobs in B-sched-defaults), B-quota-* and B-af-* (job budgets and quota awareness use them), B-bugs-fix-now and B-upstream-detectors (trigger sources/actions), T-* robustness tasks (the 'fill check' job). Constraints from this project's history: MCP tools/list byte budget is nearly full, so ONE ddflow_schedule tool with an action argument (verbs for jobs and triggers); strict fold needs every new event kind registered with its first writer; hot files cli.py, mcp.py, config.py, model.py are contended, so put parsers in their own command module (add_schedule_parser) and keep edits there minimal; every verb needs CLI + MCP twin + parity row + README row + help group + tests that fail before.

## P-security-gate — Security gate: scan for security issues, check and upgrade dependencies, enforce security and corporate policy

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/26 tasks · 3 abandoned

> Research R-security-gate-design. Adds a default 'security' gate to the task and phase pipelines. Reuse, do not duplicate: the scanners ci already runs (bandit, gitleaks, pip-audit) move behind ONE shared runner that both the gate and ci call; SECURITY-related queue items B-security-pass (phase-level gate, cadence, companions), B-dependency-upgrades, B-security-pass-sync, B-export-security-md, B-pi-review-lens (security lens) and IA-supply-chain overlap this phase: SEC-decide asks the operator whether this phase supersedes or absorbs them, and nothing here edits those items. A scanner that cannot run is recorded unavailable, never passed. Corporate policy rides the company layer (D-config-layer-order): tighten-only floors, expiring waivers (D-DEP-Q8). This project pins [gates].task_pipeline literally in .ddflow/config.toml, so the gate must also be added there.

The method is reproduced with the best available models; the real Mythos model is not available. The timing decision (phase only versus also on risky diffs) is SEC-hunt-decide's question.

## P-session-context — Session context: a session tree, addressed transfer between sessions and agents, native lane state, and using VS Code multi-chat / Claude Code / Projects with ddflow

`open` · ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 0/4 tasks · 1 abandoned · needs `P-agent-memory`, `P-docs-generic`, `P-roadmap`, `P-docs-search`

> Operator request 2026-10-11 (verbatim): "Look at this new features (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions#_run-multiple-chats-in-a-session) - vscode capability to have sessions, subsessions, transfer of context between sessions, research also the claude project concept which seems to be something similar. Make a research if some of those ideas could be reused to extend the functionality and capability of the ddflow tool, how do we share context between sessions, subsessions and agents, also could we separately take advantage of these new features too. If you find any gaps it is worth for us to work on - add them in a respective phase + tasks"

> Evidence: R-session-context (THEORETICAL: vendor docs read through a summarising fetch) and R-session-context-adopt (CONFIRMED: adopt for vscode/copilot writes no .github/agents, prompts, hooks, instructions).

> FINDING: most of the idea is ALREADY on the roadmap and is NOT refiled here: capture of briefs/reports (B-am-capture), structured session.handoff and round-trip verify (B-am-handoff), restart brief with see-also (B-am-restart-brief), search over old context (B-am-search), session CLI (B-am-session-cli), Claude transcript ingest (B-am-ingest), lane ledger (B-gap-lanes), subagent registry and sync (P-subagents), hook writers per harness (B-hx-hook-writers), command directories (B-adopt-agent-commands), project knowledge = ddflow brief + decisions + rules + memory + exports (a Claude-Projects-like project instructions/memory already exists and is more selective: glob-ranked, fenced, budgeted). This phase files ONLY what is missing: (1) a session TREE (parent link, role, goal, outcome) - sessions have no parent today; (2) an addressed TRANSFER/fork pack between sessions and agents, rendered for any harness; (3) lane STATE from the harness's own listing (claude agents --json) and ddflow-session to native-session mapping with the exact resume line; (4) a practical guide for using VS Code multi-chat, Claude Code fork/teams/Projects together with ddflow today. Extended instead of filed: B-am-harness-probe, B-sub-sync, B-adopt-agent-commands, B-hx-hook-writers (marked paragraphs).

> HOLD: this phase waits behind the same old-work hold as P-multiuser (P-gaps core: B-gap-log-scale, B-gap-lanes, B-gap-plan-lint; docs wave: P-docs-generic, P-roadmap, P-docs-search) AND after P-agent-memory, whose capture/handoff/restart-brief it builds on. B-sc-decide asks the operator first; nothing else starts before the answers.

## P-soft-upgrade — Soft upgrades: a tiny stable MCP shim owns the connection, a restartable worker holds ddflow; upgrades that keep the interface (or re-announce it) need no agent restart

`open` · ███████░░░░░░░░░░░ 9/23 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-21: detach the MCP communication section from the libraries so ddflow can be upgraded under a running agent. SOFT upgrade = applied with no agent restart and reported as such; HARD upgrade = the agent must be restarted. Re-announcing a changed tool/prompt interface to the client (list_changed) should widen what is soft. Sequenced right AFTER P-tool-diet (the tool surface must settle first: the interface digest, profiles and aliases are defined there). Research (R-soft-*): initialize takes 6-20 s today (B-mcp-initialize-folds-log), server holds ~300 MB and 158+ modules; in-process reload is unsafe (R-soft-inprocess-reload REFUTED); Claude Code 2.1.296 honours tools/list_changed incl. unsolicited, additions and removals (R-soft-claude-listchanged), a stdlib shim hot-swapping a worker works end to end (R-soft-shim-prototype); other clients (Cursor) reportedly ignore it and 2026-07-28 moves list_changed to subscriptions/listen with ttlMs caching (R-soft-client-table, THEORETICAL). Recommended: architecture A+D (shim + worker + digest-driven re-announcement), with the existing [mcp].on_upgrade=reexec kept as the fallback for hard upgrades. Definition: interface digest = sha256 over the canonical JSON of tool names/schemas/descriptions/annotations, prompt names/arguments, server instructions template id, capabilities and protocol versions. SOFT = shim and shim<->worker protocol unchanged AND (digest unchanged OR digest changed and the connected client is known to honour list_changed AND the change is additive/removal or schema-compatible with the previous schema). HARD = shim or worker protocol major changed, or the client does not honour list_changed, or an existing tool's required arguments changed incompatibly. Acceptance for the phase: an end-to-end test that upgrades a worker under a live stdio connection with an in-flight call, for each class.

## P-specs — Project specifications: a scoped, reviewed, versioned spec record (feature, design, interface, acceptance) bound to tasks and tests, with drift detection and contextual injection

`open` · ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/21 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-21 (verbatim): "Make a research of how ddflow can manage project specifications, do a deep research and check what we have, what we plan, what could be reused and make a proposition with phase and tasks with dependencies and waves for the gaps"

> Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/project-specifications.md (task SPEC-research).

> WHAT THIS PHASE IS: NATIVE, in-project specifications (feature spec, design doc, interface contract, acceptance suite) as one scoped, reviewed, versioned record whose prose stays in a file (docs/specs/*.md, a document type), bound to the tasks that implement it by digest, traced to tests, checked against code, and delivered to agent sessions by section under a budget. NOT: engineering requirements/standards (P-requirements, RQM-*), product requirements/EARS/stakeholders/RFP (P-product-docs, PD-*), spec-driven-tool import/export of Spec Kit/OpenSpec/Kiro trees (P-sdd, SDD-*), cross-project shared specs, format adapters, change requests, consumer edges (P-constellation, CN-*). The phase REUSES them: SPEC-decide proposes ONE kind `spec` that SDD-model's spec-source and CN-spec-kind become instances of (field `format`, `source`), so the three do not grow three kinds.

> REUSE (confirmed in code/queue): record contract and data kinds (done), doc types and validate/sources (done), guidance engine (scope, rank, budget, fence, dedupe), RQM-provider seam, RQM-check verify runner, RQM-trace/PD-trace suspect-link primitive, PD-baseline/CN-baseline baseline engine, plan check/apply/confirm and core.schedule waves (done), ledger digest pattern (services/ledger.py), review gate with cross-family reviewers, B-rc-changes change feed, DX-drift-notice.

> SEQUENCING: SPEC-decide carries the hold of D-old-work-behind-core-docs (it needs the P-gaps core and the docs wave); everything else waits behind it. Waves are stated in the research doc and were verified acyclic with every need existing.

## P-unify — One kernel of shared interfaces: commands, records, search, file monitoring, workers, processes, files, config, workflow and DAG declared once and reused, so new features are data and the bug surface shrinks

`done` · ██████████████████ 217/217 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-05 (verbatim in session s20260929T144138-2948413): research the software and propose a phase for a generic refactoring and unified interfaces for search, file monitoring, processing, CLI, MCP, RAG, indexing, workflow, DAG, optimisation; best libraries; what to refactor and optimise; minimise the code surface; more shared and reusable code with a smaller bug surface; account for planned work. Research R-unify (CONFIRMED; measured on main e4342e62, 73.4k lines). FINDINGS: concerns solved many ways rather than copy-pasted -- commands declared 3x (build_parser 1,229 lines, mcp.TOOLS ~2,670, commands/* ~4,400), 6 rankers/4 tokenizers/7 slug helpers, 6 git wrappers + 22 raw git calls + 7 shell runners (5 leave orphans), 4 atomic writers + 33 plain writes of important files, 4 TOML emitters, 5 region writers, 4 definitions of 'gate settled', 6 DAG walks, 167 knobs declared twice with 21 enums unchecked, 9 clippers, 2 redactors; and ~281 open tasks would add ~12 CRUD surfaces, ~9 asset loaders, ~8 definition-record families, 5 trigger evaluators, 4-5 tick mechanisms, 3 limiters, 2 embedding backends, 6 context injectors, ~10 command runners. Four bugs found and filed (fix-Bed0f5b6d99 orphaned children on timeout, fix-B28cab0652a rule TOML quoting, fix-Beea0744a7b unchecked enum knobs, fix-B9c56de9d58 non-ASCII ls-files) -- fixed first, bugs-first. LIBRARIES (policy for B-uni-decide): core stays Jinja2; vendor tomlkit for comment-preserving config writes; optional extras with stdlib fallbacks and a doctor probe: [search] rapidfuzz, [watch] watchfiles, [rag] model2vec+sqlite-vec, [mcp-sdk] only for HTTP; stdlib graphlib, FTS5 trigram, git merge-file, subprocess git; dev-only hypothesis, syrupy, import-linter, mutmut; avoid pydantic/FastMCP in core, GitPython/pygit2/dulwich, merge3 (GPL), atomicwrites, networkx at runtime. METHOD: strangler -- each interface lands with a ratchet test counting the old call sites, which only goes down; behaviour is pinned first by golden/property tests; no task changes user-visible behaviour except the bug fixes. BUILDS ON (does not duplicate): B-hot-files splits (B-split-mcp-tools, -cli-parser, -config, -model-handlers, -api-lifecycle), B-relpath-helper, B-json-failures, B149 (MCP 2026-07-28), B-coh-coverage, B-id-generator, B-trigger-model/B-sched-model, B-hx-descriptor/B-hx-hook-core, B-tpl-regions, B-view-list-core (done), B-export-core (done). `done` · ██████████████████ 27/27 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-09 (relayed by the coordinator): DO THE CLEANUP BEFORE THE PAUSE -- migrate the remaining call sites onto the shared interfaces and delete the old code. Constraints: no feature loss (golden snapshots and the full suite stay green, pinned before and after as every P-unify slice did); the compat aliases/deprecations that D-compat keeps until 1.0 stay; the work adds no new feature.

> Why: P-unify finished with ddflow/ at 104,929 lines (393 modules), +43% against the 73,400 recorded in R-unify, against a -10% target (research R-unify-acceptance, REFUTED). The interfaces exist; call sites were migrated slice by slice; the old code was not all deleted.

> The plan and its measured inventory are research R-unify-cleanup-plan. Realistic target (not -10%): ddflow/ about 102,700 lines (commit to <= 103,300; -2%), tests about 118,500 (-1,000); ratchets: subprocess_calls 13->4, write_text 10->0, tempfile 6->0, deferred_imports 534->90, surfaces-through-api 34->6, subprocess-home 7->1, fsio-home 7->1, complexity_d_or_worse 100->85 (F-grade 5->2), duplicate_code_clusters 4->0, unreferenced_functions 5->2. -10% of the original (66,060 lines) would need -38,869 lines (-37%) which only removing features could give; B-uc-acceptance says so plainly with the measurement.

> Structure: 18 slices with disjoint file globs (by package or ratchet). Wave 1, ready at once: B-uc-guard-split (0.5 d, unblocks the three import-linter lanes), the three api slices, B-uc-core-views, the five services slices, B-uc-deps-comments. After the guard split: B-uc-infra-proc-fsio, B-uc-mcp, B-uc-surf-registry. After B-uc-surf-registry: the four B-uc-surf-* family slices. ## P-user-stories — User requirements and user stories: personas, epics, stories with testable acceptance criteria, readiness and done checks, clarifying questions, story-to-plan-to-test traceability

`open` · █░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 2/26 tasks

> Operator 2026-10-21 (verbatim): "Make a research how ddflow could manage user requirements and user stories, for a project - make a deep research what are the best practices, what we do, what we plan to do, what can be reused, and make a phase and tasks proposal for the implementation with dependencies and wave set"

> SCOPE: the USER-FACING layer only: user/business needs, personas, epics, stories, acceptance criteria, splitting, prioritisation, Definition of Ready/Done, release grouping, and the flow idea -> clarifying questions -> story -> readiness -> plan apply -> tasks -> verify criteria -> done. Siblings (link, do not duplicate): P-requirements (engineering standards, shipped requirement kind, D-requirements-*), P-product-docs (requirement record with EARS text, stakeholders, baselines, lint, trace, scoring, doc types), AP-stories (autopilot: stories -> a phase of tasks within a budget), P-specs (functional/technical specs, if filed by res-specs). Evidence and design: docs/ddflow/research/user-stories.md (task US-research).

## P-zcode — ZCode (Z.ai) at full harness parity: verified descriptor, hooks, session identity, lane driver, skills and conformance

`open` · ██░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 1/10 tasks
